title: Quantum-Inspired Neural Network Architectures for Symbolic Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-inspired neural network architectures for enhancing symbolic computation. Traditional neural networks often struggle with the inherent structure and logical reasoning required in symbolic tasks. We propose a novel framework leveraging principles from quantum mechanics—specifically non-locality and entanglement—to design neural networks that can more effectively perform symbolic manipulation and reasoning. The core idea involves introducing non-local connections and mimicking entanglement-like interactions within the network architecture. This approach aims to overcome limitations of conventional neural networks by incorporating probabilistic and interconnected representations reminiscent of quantum systems. The resulting architectures, termed Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks (QINNs), are hypothesized to offer improved efficiency and accuracy in symbolic computation, potentially bridging the gap between classical computation and quantum processing paradigms. We outline the key architectural components and theoretical underpinnings of QINNs, focusing on how they translate quantum concepts into a neural network setting. The goal is to demonstrate a viable pathway for harnessing quantum-inspired ideas to tackle complex symbolic problems.

The core idea involves introducing non-local connections and mimicking entanglement-like interactions within the network architecture. This approach aims to overcome limitations of conventional neural networks by incorporating probabilistic and interconnected representations reminiscent of quantum systems. The resulting architectures, termed Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks (QINNs), are hypothesized to offer improved efficiency and accuracy in symbolic computation, potentially bridging the gap between classical computation and quantum processing paradigms. We outline the key architectural components and theoretical underpinnings of QINNs, focusing on how they translate quantum concepts into a neural network setting. The goal is to demonstrate a viable pathway for harnessing quantum-inspired ideas to tackle complex symbolic problems.

title: Quantum Entanglement Optimization via Adaptive Topological Structures
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge for information processing and communication. While the phenomenon itself is well-established, the practical application of entanglement often necessitates efficient and stable protocols. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum entanglement optimization, utilizing adaptive topological structures to dynamically adjust the entanglement's structure. We propose a new algorithm, dubbed "Adaptive Topological Optimization," which leverages a self-organized network of topological defects to enhance entanglement fidelity and robustness. This method offers a pathway toward more efficient and stable entanglement generation and manipulation. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating a dynamic network of topological defects, which in turn influence the entanglement's properties. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, demonstrates its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, and provides insights into potential future research directions.

title: Probabilistic Programming with Bayesian Monte Carlo Tree Search
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of probabilistic programming with Bayesian Monte Carlo Tree Search (BMCTS). The core claim is that BMCTS can be significantly enhanced by leveraging the capabilities of probabilistic programming to improve both accuracy and efficiency in exploring the search space. The proposed mechanism combines the strengths of BMCTS – its ability to efficiently explore vast search spaces – with a probabilistic programming system, enabling the agent to learn and maintain a probability distribution over the possible actions and their associated outcomes. This allows for a more nuanced and adaptive exploration strategy, moving beyond purely heuristic-based approaches. We demonstrate that this integration results in a more robust and performant search algorithm. The key innovation lies in embedding Bayesian inference directly within the BMCTS framework, leading to improved exploration and ultimately, better decision-making.

title: Formal Verification of Secure Multi-Party Computation Protocols via Symbolic Execution
abstract: Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) enables computations on sensitive data without revealing individual inputs. However, ensuring the security of MPC protocols – verifying that no party can learn information beyond what is explicitly intended – remains a significant challenge. This work proposes a novel approach to formal verification of MPC protocols using symbolic execution. We leverage symbolic execution to generate a precise, executable specification of the protocol's behavior, allowing for automated verification of security properties. The core of our method involves a symbolic execution engine that systematically explores all possible execution paths of the MPC protocol, creating a symbolic representation of the computation. This representation is then rigorously checked against the desired security guarantees. Our approach automates a traditionally manual and error-prone process, offering a substantial improvement in security assurance for MPC protocols. We demonstrate the applicability and effectiveness of this technique through a detailed analysis of a simplified, yet representative, MPC protocol. The results highlight the potential of automated verification to bolster the trustworthiness of MPC systems.

title: Quantum Logic Gate Design and Optimization: Based on Topological Quantum Effects
abstract: This paper explores the design and optimization of quantum logic gates leveraging the principles of topological quantum effects. The core claim is that exploiting these effects allows for the creation of quantum logic gates with significantly enhanced fidelity compared to traditional approaches. The central mechanism involves constructing quantum devices based on topological quantum effects, utilizing their inherent properties to perform logical operations. The novelty lies in the paradigm shift offered by topological effects as a new route for quantum logic gate design. We will detail the theoretical framework, focusing on the manipulation of Majorana zero modes (MZMs) – a key element of topological quantum computing – to realize fundamental quantum gates such as the CNOT and Toffoli gates. Mathematical formulations will be presented to describe the gate operations and the resulting fidelity, demonstrating the potential advantages. Furthermore, we will discuss challenges and future directions for the practical implementation of these gates.

title: DARD: Zero-Shot Degradation-Aware Retinex-Guided Diffusion for Low-Light Image Enhancement
abstract: Existing diffusion-based enhancement methods provide strong generative capability for low-light image enhancement (LLIE), yet they either rely on paired supervision or lack reliable scene constraints in zero-shot settings, often leading to structural inconsistency and color drift. Motivated by conventional Retinex models, which offer physically interpretable priors that can serve as reliable scene constraints yet struggle with mixed degradations in real-world scenarios, we propose DARD, a zero-shot Degradation-Aware Retinex-guided Diffusion framework for LLIE. DARD first extracts image-specific physical priors from the degraded input through a test-time degradation-aware Retinex decomposition, thereby providing reliable structural guidance for zero-shot restoration. It then injects these priors into reverse diffusion through a timestep-adaptive frequency fusion strategy to balance structural anchoring and detail generation. Finally, a guided reverse refinement process with physical consistency and Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP)-based semantic guidance is introduced to suppress structural artifacts and semantic drift during sampling. Extensive experiments show that DARD achieves strong distortion and perceptual performance and consistently outperforms existing zero-shot baselines across multiple real-world low-light benchmarks. To further validate the practical utility of our method for downstream applications, we evaluated its impact on semantic segmentation. Experiments demonstrate that images enhanced by DARD achieve a 28.10% relative improvement in mIoU over AGLLDiff.

title: Green Edge AI for Cyber-Physical Systems: Stream-Native Topological Isolation against Adversarial Attacks in Resource-Constrained IoT
abstract: Legacy $O(N)$ and $O(\log N)$ machine learning architectures encounter severe thermodynamic and geometrical limitations within large-scale artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) deployments. The Event Horizon - Decoupled Quartic-Gated (EH-DQG) framework, driven by a Cholesky-Gated Momentum (CGM) engine, resolves the stability-plasticity dilemma in resource-constrained environments. The architecture isolates anomalies in a whitened topological phase space. Stream-native execution achieves a strict per-packet time and space complexity of $O(d^2)$. Empirical hardware profiling on proxy microcontrollers demonstrates a practical engineering trade-off. The deterministic engine utilizes a peak working memory footprint of 4,176 Bytes and maintains a core state dimension of 456 Bytes. Algorithmic execution yields an empirically verified 11.19-year hardware-bounded autonomy limit. Thermodynamic expenditure requires a marginal energy penalty compared to static legacy models. The framework mathematically bounds adversarial vulnerabilities despite the minor resource exchange. The restrictive hyper-ellipse reduces maximum achievable physical damage from 18.00 down to 0.90. High resilience against gradual poisoning and manifold-targeted evasion is consequently ensured. A density-driven phase shift mechanism guarantees instantaneous recovery from abrupt concept drift without succumbing to catastrophic deadlocks. The proposed architecture ultimately provides a mathematically bounded, scalable Green Edge AI foundation for mission-critical cyber-physical systems, including deep-space constellations and implantable biomedical devices.

title: Accretive Computing Multi-Agent System
abstract: Accretive Computing: A Physics-Driven Paradigm for Continuous Multi-Agent Orchestration Traditional Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) rely on discrete, hard-coded directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) that suffer from an O(N^2) routing bottleneck and lack spontaneous discovery. This paper introduces Accretive Computing, a novel computational paradigm that replaces rigid von Neumann routing with a continuous topological physics engine. By modeling AI agents as oscillating wave functions in an N-dimensional semantic substrate, agent orchestration is organically governed by fundamental physical laws: wave interference, spatial proximity, and thermodynamic Free Energy minimization. Key Innovations Detailed in this Paper: Continuous Semantic Topology: Replaces explicit graph edges with topological potential wells and constructive wave-function interference. Analytical RBF Overlap: Derives a precise Gaussian Radial Basis Function (RBF) integral to solve the Curse of Dimensionality in high-dimensional latent spaces. Massive Scalability: Implements a multipole expansion spatial partitioning algorithm, reducing algorithmic simulation complexity to O(NlogN) to support swarms of up to 10,000 agents. Token Efficiency: Achieves up to a 5,000x reduction in Large Language Model (LLM) token consumption by dynamically isolating orthogonal operational states. Repository Artifacts: This upload contains the foundational architectural whitepaper for the framework. The executable hybrid C++/Python framework discussed in this manuscript is fully open-source and available for installation via PyPI, with the core engine repository hosted on GitHub. https://pypi.org/project/accretive-mas/ https://github.com/chinu3d/accretive-computing-mas-framework.git

title: Nonlinear Geometric Field Theory: A Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation framework based on non-linear geometric field theory, designed to model complex physical systems exhibiting non-linear geometric behavior. The core mechanism focuses on explicitly incorporating geometric properties into the simulation process, providing a more comprehensive representation of these systems. The research explores the potential applications of this framework within quantum information processing, leveraging the unique characteristics of non-linear geometry. This work aims to advance our understanding of the interplay between geometric dynamics and quantum information.

title: Non-Adaptive Control of Asymmetric Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of adaptive control techniques for asymmetric quantum computation. Asymmetric quantum computation, leveraging the inherent differences in qubit properties, presents a promising approach to enhance computational efficiency. However, the precise control required for these computations is notoriously challenging. This work proposes a framework where quantum measurement outcomes are continuously fed back to dynamically adjust the parameters of the quantum circuit. This adaptive control mechanism aims to mitigate the control complexity and, consequently, improve both the efficiency and accuracy of the computation. The core claim is that adaptive control significantly elevates the performance of asymmetric quantum computation. The proposed method addresses a critical bottleneck in this field – the difficulty in achieving precise control – thereby opening avenues for more robust and effective quantum algorithms. We present a theoretical model outlining this process, focusing on the feedback loop and its impact on the overall computational outcome. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the potential for improved resource utilization and reduced error rates.

title: Quantum Neural Networks: Dynamic Topology Control
abstract: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) represent a promising paradigm shift in artificial intelligence, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to enhance computational capabilities. This paper explores the concept of dynamic topology control within QNNs, focusing on the design of a novel architecture that dynamically adjusts the network's topology to optimize learning and expressiveness. We propose a quantum neural network architecture incorporating a self-adaptive topology, achieved through the manipulation of quantum states. This dynamic adjustment allows the network to learn and represent data more effectively than traditional neural networks, offering potential improvements in both accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism hinges on the application of quantum state transformations to dynamically shape the network's topology, fostering a more flexible and adaptable learning process. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the benefits of this approach, showcasing increased model performance and a novel approach to represent data.

title: 基于物理定律的进化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm (EA) inspired by fundamental physical laws. The core concept is to treat individuals within the EA as physical systems governed by principles such as thermodynamics, mechanics, and statistical mechanics. This approach leverages the inherent constraints, energy transfer mechanisms, and interactions found in physical systems to enhance the algorithm's exploration capabilities and accelerate convergence. Traditional EAs often struggle with high-dimensional and non-smooth optimization problems due to their reliance on purely stochastic search strategies. By incorporating physical laws, this new EA aims to overcome these limitations, offering a more robust and efficient solution. The algorithm utilizes simulation techniques to model the interactions between individuals and defines the fitness function based on the physical behavior of these simulated systems. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in performance compared to standard EAs across a range of benchmark problems.

title: Adaptive Machine Learning: A Dynamic Gradient Descent Strategy
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive machine learning approach utilizing a dynamically adjusted learning rate and gradient size. Traditional gradient descent methods struggle to effectively handle complex data distributions and nonlinear relationships, often requiring extensive tuning. Our proposed strategy, termed "Dynamic Gradient Descent," automatically adjusts these parameters based on data characteristics and the computational process, leading to improved model generalization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through simulations and a simplified case study, showcasing its ability to navigate challenging scenarios and achieve superior performance compared to standard gradient descent. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors data distribution and gradients, adapting the learning rate and gradient magnitude to optimize model convergence. This results in a more robust and efficient training process, particularly for data exhibiting non-linear dependencies.

title: Hyperparameter Optimization via Evolutionary Algorithms with Simulated Annealing-Inspired Transitions
abstract: Hyperparameter optimization is a critical step in the development and deployment of machine learning models. Traditional evolutionary algorithms (EAs) can struggle to escape local optima, leading to suboptimal model performance. This work proposes a novel approach that integrates simulated annealing (SA) principles into an EA framework to enhance hyperparameter tuning. The core idea is to introduce "uphill" transitions, allowing the EA to occasionally explore regions beyond local optima. These transitions are governed by a dynamically adjusted temperature parameter, mimicking the thermal fluctuations in SA. This combined methodology aims to improve the algorithm's ability to converge to the global optimum, resulting in better model performance. The evaluation is performed through simulations and theoretical analysis, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Probability Logic Computing: Adaptive Complexity Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probability logic computing based on adaptive complexity analysis. Traditional complexity analysis methods often rely on manual effort, hindering efficiency. We propose a method that transforms complexity analysis into probabilistic models, utilizing probability distributions to quantify the complexity and error of the computation process. The core mechanism involves automatically identifying critical points of complexity based on probabilistic models. This offers a significant improvement in efficiency and provides optimized recommendations for complex computations. We detail the methodology, demonstrate its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discuss future research directions.

title: Decentralized Verification of Differential Privacy using Blockchain
abstract: This paper proposes a novel decentralized verification system for differential privacy leveraging blockchain technology. Existing decentralized verification protocols for differential privacy suffer from vulnerabilities to collusion attacks, where malicious actors can compromise the privacy guarantees. Our system addresses this issue by establishing a distributed network of 'witness' nodes, each independently verifying the privacy compliance of a data processing algorithm. Crucially, these proofs are immutably recorded on a blockchain, creating a transparent and auditable trail. The system's architecture provides enhanced resilience against collusion due to the distributed nature of the verification process and the cryptographic security of the blockchain. This approach offers a practical solution for ensuring differential privacy in decentralized environments. The core mechanism involves witness nodes performing independent verification and creating cryptographic proofs. The blockchain then serves as an immutable ledger, guaranteeing the integrity of the verification process. This design significantly reduces the risk of malicious actors manipulating the verification results.

title: Analisis Sentimen Berbasis SHAP untuk Mendukung Perencanaan Strategis Sistem Layanan M-Paspor
abstract: Transformasi digital layanan publik melalui aplikasi M-Paspor menghadapi tantangan signifikan terkait stabilitas sistem dan kepuasan pengguna. Melalui pendekatan Explainable AI, metode SHAP diimplementasikan untuk membongkar mekanisme internal algoritma XGBoost, untuk mengidentifikasi kontributor utama sentimen negatif secara visual dan terukur. Berdasarkan hasil algoritma XGBoost dengan akurasi 92%, melalui pendekatan XAI dengan metode SHAP. Penelitian ini mengintegrasikan model XGBoost dengan metode SHAP yang menghasilkan identifikasi kuantitatif fitur dominan. Kata positif yaitu “lancar” (1,80), “mantap” (1,22), “membantu” (1,02) serta kata negatif “lambat” (-0,77), “mempersulit” (-0,73), “buruk” (-0,43), yang mengindikasikan adanya kendala pada sistem verifikasi dan alur antarmuka. Temuan ini selanjutnya diformulasikan ke dalam kerangka kerja strategis yang merekomendasikan prioritas perbaikan pada aspek kecepatan respons sistem, penyederhanaan prosedur, dan stabilitas teknis, yang terbukti sebagai pemicu utama sentimen negatif pada nilai SHAP: lambat = -0,77, mempersulit = -0,73, buruk = -0,43, sehingga instansi dapat meningkatkan kualitas pelayanan publik digital secara lebih terarah dan berorientasi pada pengguna.

evidence.abstract: Transformasi digital layanan publik melalui aplikasi M-Paspor menghadapi tantangan signifikan terkait stabilitas sistem dan kepuasan pengguna. Melalui pendekatan Explainable AI, metode SHAP diimplementasikan untuk membongkar mekanisme internal algoritma XGBoost, untuk mengidentifikasi kontributor utama sentimen negatif secara visual dan terukur. Berdasarkan hasil algoritma XGBoost dengan akurasi 92%, melalui pendekatan XAI dengan metode SHAP. Penelitian ini mengintegrasikan model XGBoost dengan metode SHAP yang menghasilkan identifikasi kuantitatif fitur dominan. Kata positif yaitu “lancar” (1,80), “mantap” (1,22), “membantu” (1,02) serta kata negatif “lambat” (-0,77), “mempersulit” (-0,73), “buruk” (-0,43), yang mengindikasikan adanya kendala pada sistem verifikasi dan alur antarmuka. Temuan ini selanjutnya diformulasikan ke dalam kerangka kerja strategis yang merekomendasikan prioritas perbaikan pada aspek kecepatan respons sistem, penyederhanaan prosedur, dan stabilitas teknis, yang terbukti sebagai pemicu utama sentimen negatif pada nilai SHAP: lambat = -0,77, mempersulit = -0,73, buruk = -0,43, sehingga instansi dapat meningkatkan kualitas pelayanan publik digital secara lebih terarah dan berorientasi pada pengguna.

title: Benchmark Contamination: A Taxonomy Organized by Defeated Mitigation
abstract: A benchmark score is a joint property of the model, the evaluation harness, the elicitation budget, the sampled population, and contamination status. Leaderboards publish the model and the score, so capability and leakage stay observationally equivalent. Existing taxonomies classify contamination for automated detection, not the question a reporter faces at publication: given the mitigations already applied, which validity threats remain open? We introduce a taxonomy organized by the mitigation each type defeats -- direct, derivative, temporal, distributional, and acquired -- spanning training-time and evaluation-time leakage. Holding out a private test set closes the first alone. The fifth is acquired during the evaluation itself; because it is a property of one run, it must be recorded with the reported score rather than with the benchmark release. We operationalize it as a four-field disclosure protocol in which "unknown" is a valid entry, released under CC BY 4.0 with a JSON Schema, a validator, and worked examples. Two coders external to the design team applied a pre-registered instrument to 41 documents. Per-variable linear-weighted $κ$ runs from 0.00 to 0.35 (median 0.21) over 29 main-pass documents against a single-coder test-retest ceiling of 0.84, collapsing under the class skew the registration anticipated; pooling raises it to 0.46 through chance correction rather than better agreement. Two variables fall below the prevalence-robust threshold registered in advance: strata reporting and the acquired type introduced here. Disagreement concentrates on when a variable applies rather than on what a document states. Elicitation budgets are reported in 13% of documents, and no document addresses all five types. The contribution is the taxonomy, the score-side artifact that follows from it, and a pre-registered measurement of instrument reliability and current disclosure.

title: Formal Translation of the Empathic Logic Model into a Python Library
abstract: This extension of ELM presents the formal python translation of the Empathic Logic Model (ELM). Because foundational psychological mechanisms and narrative elements function as qualitative components, all related constructs are designated as such; for comprehensive qualitative frameworks, readers can reference the **NOT_IMPLEMENTED** sections documentation in the primary manuscript via Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18614652 ### Note on this Python Library Scope and Evaluation: Python Library Scope and Operational Interpretation. ELM is an applied computational architecture for dynamic interactive systems, evaluated through operational execution, transition robustness, fault tolerance, and recovery, including adversarial stress testing under Full-Stack Turing Deadlock, PBFT, and ABFT-inspired conditions, rather than abstract mathematical proofs. Its architecture is not intrinsically limited to human–human interaction and may be instantiated in human–machine interaction, machine-learning pipelines, AI safety, robotics, autonomous systems, and other interactive agents, subject to implementation and empirical validation. Artificial intelligence systems were utilized in the formalization and Python translation presented herein. ###Future Translation Note: Its translation into engineering architectures remains open to domain-specific implementation, with the resulting configurations determined by the requirements and operational constraints of each application field and informed by subsequent empirical development. ### Library and Execution Note: The resulting Python implementation may be used as an ELM computational library, with application-specific execution blocks constructed by implementers according to the requirements and operational constraints of their respective systems. ###Explanation of this Library: ELM governs the interpretation process by determining what the system should do next with received input and how that input should be handled. The input may originate from a sensory parser or other data parser in machine systems, or from biological sensory organs in human beings. By operating directly after the input layer of a system, ELM provides a structured mechanism for managing interpretation toward understanding rather than premature judgment, contextual data rather than static guessing, and the detection and resolution of uncertainty and predictive errors. This includes both preventing and resolving predictive errors—ELM helps identify the triggers of predictive errors and resolve them to prevent the errors from occurring in the first place—as well as helping to resolve predictive errors when others commit them. ELM examines whether the received input contains sufficient contextual information, insufficient contextual information, or distorted contextual information. When contextual information is unavailable or distorted, ELM routes the system toward obtaining or refining the required contextual information through the appropriate contextual-extraction and interaction processes, while maintaining the safeguards specified by the ELM architecture to avoid introducing further predictive errors into the interaction. When the input already contains sufficient contextual information, or when missing contextual information has been obtained through the appropriate extraction and refinement processes established in ELM, ELM subjects the resulting contextual information to the verification and stabilization processes defined by its architecture. When the relevant criteria are satisfied, the resulting information can then be made available to the system for its application-specific purpose. ELM does not impose artificial agreement and does not seek to eliminate disagreement. It prioritizes proportional coherence over certainty, clarity over control, and understanding over judgment. Accordingly, ELM provides an end-to-end computational routing architecture for the interpretation process within the operational scope defined by its formal specification, including contextual assessment, contextual acquisition and refinement, verification, stabilization, state transitions, interruption handling, and recovery. This allows systems such as human beings, corporations, institutions, robots, artificial intelligence systems, machine-learning pipelines, autonomous systems, and other interactive agents to operate on contextually processed and verified information rather than relying solely on static guessing or unverified input, subject to their respective implementation requirements and empirical validation.

title: Dynamic Multi-State Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper presents a novel computational framework for simulating complex multi-state quantum systems, leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum tunneling to model system evolution. Traditional multi-state simulation methods often struggle with the intricacies of multi-body dynamics. We propose a framework that explicitly incorporates quantum entanglement and tunneling as fundamental mechanisms for simulating the evolution of quantum systems. This framework offers improved accuracy and scalability for simulating systems exhibiting complex, non-linear dynamics, providing a significant advancement in quantum computing.

title: Graph Embeddings for Predicting Scientific Discovery
abstract: Predicting scientific discovery is a significant challenge, demanding the ability to discern nascent research ideas from established knowledge. This work explores the application of graph embeddings – a technique prevalent in fields like social network analysis and natural language processing – to the domain of scientific discovery. We hypothesize that relationships between scientific concepts, as represented by citation networks, can be effectively encoded using graph embeddings. These embeddings can then serve as powerful features in predictive models designed to assess the likelihood of future breakthroughs. Our approach involves training graph embedding models, specifically Node2Vec, on citation networks, thereby capturing complex interconnections between research areas. Experimental results (simulated, due to the lack of real-world experimental data) demonstrate the potential of this method for identifying promising research directions. The core contribution lies in the novel application of graph embedding techniques to accelerate scientific research by providing a mechanism for proactive discovery prediction. This research provides a foundation for future work exploring diverse scientific domains and incorporating additional data sources.

title: 自适应量子测量协议的量子自适应性
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum measurement protocol designed for adaptive quantum measurement. Traditional methods often rely on static parameter settings, limiting the potential for optimizing measurement precision and efficiency. This research proposes a quantum self-adaptive protocol that dynamically adjusts measurement parameters in response to the evolution of the quantum state. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, highlighting its ability to significantly improve measurement accuracy and efficiency compared to static methods. The core mechanism leverages quantum state evolution to achieve this adaptive control. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the protocol, including its mathematical formulation and implementation details.

title: Title: Formal Verification of Abstract Group Theory via Constraint Relaxation
abstract: Abstract group theory, a foundational area of mathematics, presents significant challenges for formal verification due to its inherent complexity and sensitivity to subtle variations. Traditional verification methods often struggle to encompass the full scope of possible states, leading to incomplete or inaccurate results. This paper explores a novel constraint relaxation technique designed to address these limitations, moving beyond traditional proof-by-induction to enable more robust and automated verification. We introduce a probabilistic constraint relaxation process that intelligently explores configurations, maintaining high confidence levels. This approach offers a promising pathway towards verifying the stability of abstract group theory, with potential implications for cryptography and number theory.

title: Adaptive Symbol Generation and Reasoning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to symbol generation and reasoning, addressing the limitations of traditional, static symbol systems. The core idea is to construct a system capable of automatically generating and reasoning with symbols, adapting its representation and inference rules based on environmental changes and task demands. We achieve this through a combined mechanism leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Reinforcement Learning (RL). A generator network, trained using GANs, learns to produce symbol representations, while an RL agent optimizes the generator's reasoning capabilities. The resulting adaptive system offers increased flexibility and intelligence in symbol processing, particularly suited for complex and dynamic environments. This work demonstrates a foundational architecture for intelligent symbol manipulation, moving beyond fixed representations to truly dynamic reasoning.

title: Quantum Computation Resource Scheduling and Optimization Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework for resource scheduling and optimization within quantum computing. The core claim is to establish a method capable of optimally allocating quantum resources based on the specific characteristics of quantum programs and the constraints imposed by hardware limitations. The proposed approach leverages linear programming and combinatorial optimization techniques to formulate a quantum computation resource scheduling model. An algorithm is designed to optimize this model, ultimately leading to efficient resource utilization. The research addresses a complex and evolving area of quantum computing, aiming to provide a foundational theory for practical quantum resource management. The key contribution lies in the development of a tailored optimization model that considers the unique demands of quantum algorithms and the inherent limitations of quantum hardware. This work lays the groundwork for future advancements in quantum computation by offering a systematic approach to resource allocation.

title: Dynamic Kernel Learning for Adaptive Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm, Dynamic Kernel Learning (DKL), designed to enhance the performance of RL agents in complex environments. DKL addresses the limitations of traditional RL methods that often rely on fixed kernel functions for value estimation. The core innovation lies in the continuous adaptation of the kernel function itself through a meta-learning approach. A dedicated neural network learns to adjust the kernel parameters, such as the bandwidth of a Gaussian kernel, based on the agent's reward signals and state transitions. This dynamic adaptation allows the agent to effectively generalize across diverse states and improve exploration efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DKL through theoretical analysis and outline its key components and training procedure. The algorithm offers a promising direction for improving the robustness and adaptability of RL agents, particularly in scenarios with high-dimensional state spaces and non-stationary environments. The key benefit is the ability to tailor the value function representation to the current state of the environment, leading to faster convergence and better final performance.

title: Title: Topological Quantum Entanglement Networks (TQEN)
abstract: This paper explores the design and implementation of Topological Quantum Entanglement Networks (TQEN) – a novel framework for constructing and manipulating entanglement across complex topological networks. The core claim is that entanglement, treated as a fundamental resource, can be strategically leveraged to create robust and scalable quantum information processing systems. We introduce a dynamically adjustable topology based on graph theory and fractal geometry, enabling the formation of entanglement pathways with enhanced resilience and scalability. This approach departs from traditional entanglement protocols, focusing on the *structure* of entanglement rather than simply manipulating its properties. The resulting TQEN architecture promises significant advancements in quantum computation and data storage, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for leveraging entanglement as a crucial resource.

title: Heterogeneous Stacking Ensemble with Hybrid Resampling for Imbalanced Multi-label Classification
abstract: Multi-label Classification (MLC) has become crucial in various real-world applications, but its performance is often influenced by complex data imbalance issues, inter-label dependencies, and label concurrency.The imbalance in MLC is much more complicated than in single-label classification because minority labels often appear alongside majority labels, leading to model bias.This research proposes an extended hybrid resampling architecture combined with a Heterogeneous Stacking Ensemble to address these issues.This methodology begins with a two-stage hybrid resampling technique: first, using the R-HwR-ROS and R-HwR-SMT for label decoupling and dataset reconstruction to reduce concurrency.Second, applying the Multi-Label edited Nearest Neighbor (MLeNN) module for noise filtering and Multi-Label Tomek Link (MLTL) for borderline refinement.In the classification stage, three heterogeneous paradigms are used as base learners: Classifier Chain (CC), Calibrated Label Ranking (CLR), and ML-kNN.The predictions from these three models are then combined using XGBoost as a meta-learner optimized to handle the complexity of inter-label relationships.Evaluation uses ten predefined outer folds, five-fold OOF probability generation, and training-only threshold selection that maximizes F1-Macro.Across eight datasets, the best E5 configuration achieved a higher best-stage value than E4 on five datasets for F1-Macro, six for F1-Micro, and all eight for Subset Accuracy; it achieved a lower Hamming Loss on seven datasets, but a higher Macro Recall on only one dataset.The exploratory across-dataset Wilcoxon-Holm comparison identified a significant E5 improvement only for Subset Accuracy (pHolm=0.0391);the F1-Macro difference was not significant (pHolm=0.4609).These findings show that stacking improves selected performance dimensions but does not uniformly improve minority-label sensitivity, so conclusions must combine F1-Macro, Macro Recall, per-label behavior, and paired statistical evidence.

title: Speckle aware attention and multi scale pooling for robust breast ultrasound lesion classification across multiple benchmarks
abstract: Breast ultrasound (BUS) is widely used for lesion assessment, yet automatic benign–malignant classification remains challenging owing to speckle noise, weak boundaries, and cross-scanner heterogeneity. We propose SUA-Net, a compact framework that augments an EfficientNet-B0 backbone with three purpose-built modules: Dual-Path Lightweight Aggregation (DLA) for multi-scale contextual refinement, Speckle Variance Attention (SVA) for variance-guided feature reweighting, and a Multi-Granularity Pooling (MGP) head for enriched global summarization. Predictive uncertainty is estimated via Monte Carlo Dropout at inference time. The full model contains 12.225M parameters and requires 0.630G MACs and 1.260G FLOPs for a 224 × 224 input, with a deterministic model-only latency of 9.708 ± 0.508 ms on an NVIDIA Tesla T4. Under five-fold cross-validation on BUSI, BUSBRA, and BUS-UCLM (image-wise for BUSI and patient-wise for BUSBRA and BUS-UCLM), SUA-Net achieved accuracy/AUC-ROC of 0.940/0.971 on BUSI, 0.870/0.909 on BUSBRA, and 0.830/0.852 on BUS-UCLM. Cross-dataset evaluation showed that BUSBRA-trained models generalised most effectively (AUC-ROC of 0.891 on BUSI and 0.899 on BUS-UCLM), and ablation analysis showed dataset-dependent contributions from DLA, SVA, and MGP. The results support variance-guided attention, lightweight aggregation, and enriched pooling within a compact BUS classification framework and support evaluation across multiple datasets.

title: Disentangling Representation using Attributes-based Gaussian Estimation for Medical Sound Diagnosis
abstract: Deep learning has a powerful capability of feature extraction. However, the lack of fairness and interpretability in deep neural networks poses limitations to their adoption in the medical domain. This paper proposes a disentangled representation learning (DisenRL) framework, named the Attributes-based Gaussian Estimation for Disentangled Representation (AGEDR), which incorporates Attribute Mapping Embedding (AME) modules designed to map attributes into vectors and align them with a subset of the latent vectors in a Variational AutoEncoder (VAE). This part of the latent vector will be disentangled from the remaining latent vectors by minimizing mutual information. A classifier is then trained using the mean parameters of the latent vectors from the VAE. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AGEDR outperforms both conventional classification models and existing disentangled representation learning methods. The ablation experiments also indicate the disentangling capability and fairness of AGEDR. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/ZhaoKe1024/DisentangledRepr.

title: Kemampuan Deskriptif LLM Terhadap Software Vulnerability: Komparasi Chatgpt, Gemini, Dan Deepseek Dalam Identifikasi CVE
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kemampuan tiga Large Language Model (LLM), yaitu ChatGPT, Gemini, dan DeepSeek, dalam menjelaskan informasi Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) secara akurat, jelas, relevan, dan mendalam melalui eksperimen komparatif berbasis prompt. Desain penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif-kualitatif dengan eksperimen komparatif, di mana model diberi serangkaian prompt terstandar terhadap kumpulan CVE yang dipilih secara kategorikal untuk memastikan variasi jenis kerentanan, tingkat keparahan, dan domain aplikasi. Respons LLM kemudian dinilai oleh minimal tiga evaluator menggunakan skala Likert (misalnya 1–5) pada dimensi-dimensi teknis seperti akurasi fakta, kedalaman penjelasan, kejelasan bahasa, relevansi informasi, serta konsistensi informasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa ChatGPT dapat menjelaskan CVE lebih baik dibandingkan Gemini dan DeepSeek dengan skor total tertinggi (3,91), diikuti Gemini (3,76), dan DeepSeek (3,52) dengan perbedaan yang signifikan. Identifikasi halusinasi dan inkonsistensi menunjukkan bahwa DeepSeek menghasilkan halusinasi yang paling tinggi dengan jenis kesalahan dan tingkat inkonsistensi substansial paling dominan. Selain itu, hasil evaluasi persepsi pengguna mengungkapkan bahwa meskipun ketiga model dinilai cukup mudah dipahami, namun tingkat kepercayaan untuk menggunakan output LLM tanpa verifikasi sangat rendah di semua platform. Hal ini mengindikasikan bahwa pengguna secara konsisten tetap memerlukan verifikasi manual sebagai langkah yang penting. Penelitian lanjutan disarankan memperluas cakupan CVE, menguji strategi prompt engineering seperti chain-of-thought prompting untuk menekan tingkat hallucination, serta membandingkan performa model versi gratis dan berbayar pada domain keamanan.

title: Quantum Computing via Modal Function Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the application of modal function theory to quantum computing, aiming to enhance the efficiency and precision of quantum algorithms. The core claim is that applying modal function theory provides a novel framework for analyzing and optimizing quantum algorithms. The mechanism involves leveraging the properties of modal functions to rigorously assess the state space evolution inherent in quantum computations, identifying bottlenecks and suggesting targeted improvements. This work explores the theoretical foundations for this approach, proposing a methodology for representing quantum algorithms as modal functions and subsequently utilizing techniques from modal logic to derive performance metrics and guide algorithmic modifications. Specifically, we examine how the concept of 'accessibility' within modal functions can be mapped to the notion of quantum measurement and decoherence, offering a potentially powerful tool for understanding and mitigating these fundamental challenges in quantum computation. The analysis presented demonstrates the potential for significant gains in algorithm execution time and fidelity, particularly for complex quantum circuits. Further research will focus on developing practical algorithms based on this theoretical framework and exploring its applicability across diverse quantum computing architectures.

title: Explainable AI (XAI) via Causal Inference and Counterfactual Analysis
abstract: Current Explainable AI (XAI) methods frequently deliver post-hoc explanations that lack a fundamental understanding of the causal relationships underpinning AI decision-making. This paper proposes a novel approach to XAI that integrates causal inference and counterfactual analysis, aiming to generate more insightful and actionable explanations. Our methodology leverages causal discovery techniques to identify the key causal factors driving a model's decisions, moving beyond merely highlighting correlations. Furthermore, we employ counterfactual analysis to simulate "what-if" scenarios, allowing us to assess the potential impact of altering specific input features and understand the sensitivity of the model. This approach provides a deeper understanding of the AI system's behavior, ultimately leading to more robust and trustworthy AI models. We demonstrate the potential of this integrated framework through conceptual arguments and a detailed outline of the proposed methodology.

title: Contextualized Probabilistic Programming
abstract: Probabilistic programming offers a powerful framework for representing and reasoning with uncertainty. However, traditional probabilistic programming approaches often struggle with complex scenarios where the underlying probability distributions are highly sensitive to contextual factors. This paper introduces a novel approach – Contextualized Probabilistic Programming – that addresses this limitation by explicitly incorporating contextual information into the probabilistic models. The core idea is to augment probabilistic programming languages with contextual variables, allowing the model parameters to dynamically adjust based on the current situation. This mechanism aims to mitigate the "curse of dimensionality" and improve the accuracy of probabilistic models in complex, context-dependent environments. The proposed framework represents a significant shift from static to dynamic, context-aware probabilistic reasoning, offering a more robust and flexible solution for a wide range of applications.

title: Particle Physics in Adaptive Computing
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum field theory (QFT) to adaptive computation, a novel approach aimed at enhancing the efficiency and precision of quantum calculations. The core claim is that a dynamically adjusted QFT framework, leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum operators, can optimize calculations based on experimental data. We introduce a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism predicated on the principles of quantum optimization. This offers a significant departure from static, computationally fixed approaches, potentially unlocking new capabilities in quantum information processing. The paper details the fundamental concepts, proposes a practical implementation, and discusses the expected outcomes and limitations of this approach.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Symbolic Representation Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to symbolic representation learning by leveraging principles of quantum mechanics within the framework of reservoir computing. Traditional reservoir computing relies on recurrent neural networks with randomly connected "reservoirs" to capture temporal dynamics. We introduce the concept of a "Quantum Reservoir," a recurrent neural network augmented with mechanisms inspired by quantum superposition and interference. The core idea is to design the reservoir's connections such that they mimic the interference patterns observed in quantum systems, allowing the network to effectively learn high-dimensional symbolic representations. We detail the architecture of the Quantum Reservoir, focusing on the dynamic weighting of connections based on interference calculations. The potential of this approach to overcome limitations in classical reservoir computing and achieve superior performance in symbolic processing tasks is explored. The theoretical framework is presented, and the underlying mathematical principles are discussed. We demonstrate the potential of this method through a conceptual design, highlighting the key components and their interactions. This work represents a significant step towards integrating quantum concepts into classical machine learning techniques, offering a promising avenue for advanced symbolic representation learning.

title: Multi-Scale Quantum Information Representation Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of multi-scale approaches to quantum information representation learning. Traditional quantum information representation methods often operate at a single scale, neglecting the inherent multi-scale nature of quantum data. We propose a framework for learning quantum information representations by decomposing the information into various scales and subsequently learning a distinct feature representation for each scale. These representations are then fused to create a comprehensive multi-scale quantum representation. We hypothesize that this multi-scale approach will enable more effective extraction and representation of key quantum information features, ultimately improving the efficiency of quantum computation. The core claim of this work is that utilizing multi-scale analysis methods can significantly enhance the effectiveness of extracting and representing crucial quantum information characteristics, leading to improved quantum computing performance. The central mechanism involves the decomposition of quantum information into distinct scales, followed by the learning of feature representations for each scale, culminating in the fusion of these representations to establish a robust multi-scale quantum information representation. This research addresses a critical limitation in current quantum information processing by acknowledging and leveraging the multi-scale properties of quantum data.

title: Temporal Graph Neural Networks with Predictive Recurrence
abstract: Existing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are fundamentally designed to operate on static graph structures, limiting their ability to capture the inherent dynamics and evolution of graphs over time. This paper introduces Temporal Graph Neural Networks (TGNNs), a novel framework that integrates predictive recurrence to enable the modeling of future graph states. TGNNs combine standard GNN layers with a recurrent neural network – specifically a state-space model – trained to predict the next node state based on the current state and the graph's adjacency matrix. This approach allows the model to learn and extrapolate future graph evolution, moving beyond passive observation of static graphs to active modeling of temporal graph dynamics. The core of TGNNs lies in generating a predictive "temporal embedding" through the RNN, which is then incorporated into the GNN's message-passing process, enhancing the model's ability to represent and predict graph changes over time. We demonstrate that this approach significantly improves performance on graph evolution prediction tasks compared to traditional GNNs.

title: Examining Dengue-related Information Diffusion on Indonesian Twitter Through Sentiment-based Network Analysis, Spatial Mapping, and Temporal Dynamics
abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited.This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025.Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions.Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98.Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values.Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles.These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis.

title: Rescheduled, not redefined: The moving plateau of old-age mortality
abstract: Whether the risk of death keeps climbing at extreme ages or levels off has divided researchers for a century. We show this conflict reflects a moving target. Using cohort data from twelve low-mortality populations, we find that mortality deceleration and plateau onset shift steadily later across cohorts born from the mid-19th to the early-20th century. The data support a plateau across the full cohort range, though evidence weakens for the youngest, incompletely observed cohorts. In these younger cohorts, deceleration begins near age 100, and the fitted plateau begins beyond age 108. Because past studies focused on different cohorts and fixed age ranges, they sampled different phases of the exact same shift. The mortality plateau has no fixed age: it has been rescheduled.

title: AGRICAM: A Track-Mounted Crop Pollination Monitoring Robot
abstract: Insect pollination is critical for global food production, yet monitoring pollinators at commercial farm scale remains a challenge. Recent advances in computer vision and deep learning have enabled detailed analysis of pollinator behaviour, but monitoring must trade-off detail against spatial coverage and human or technological resources. This paper presents the Automated Guided Robot for Insect and Crop Activity Monitoring (AGRICAM), a purpose-built robotic system designed to meet the requirements of large-scale pollination monitoring in protected cropping systems. AGRICAM operates autonomously on low-cost, easily installed track for movement along crop rows, without disrupting farm operations or insect behaviour. The platform integrates two RGB cameras, microclimate sensors, GPS and RFID modules, motion sensors, and 4G cellular network connectivity for data transmission. A web interface enables remote device configuration and scheduling. The system autonomously captures video and image data of insects' locations and local environmental conditions. These are transferred to the cloud and analysed using computer vision models to quantify pollinator visitation and spatio-temporal activity variation. We deployed the system on a commercial blueberry farm to demonstrate and test its capability. It successfully mapped insect pollination patterns across 80 m long industrial polytunnels over 30 hours. This data enabled spatial analyses of insect activity we used to confirm a uniform pollinator distribution within polytunnels, as desired by the farm management team. The data also highlighted variation of insect activity associated with time of day and microclimate. AGRICAM therefore has been shown to be a scalable, automated crop pollination monitor that can support data-driven decisions to enhance pollination management, thereby improving crop productivity and food security.

title: Hybrid Semantic Context-Enhanced Ensemble Learning for Wind Power Ramp-Event Forecasting and Uncertainty-Aware Evaluation
abstract: Wind power ramp events which are sudden, large swings in turbine output over short windows are difficult to estimate, and standard models often miss them. Hybrid forecasting approach is built which augments semantic context to ramp-event forecast. Rather than applying an extensive language model directly to predict turbine operating data, we have implemented a pipeline where turbine operating data is converted to simplified text, which is then converted to dense embeddings to be used as inputs for ensemble models incorporated with other features. Testing runs are performed at multiple intervals within the SDWPF dataset, including 10-minute, 30-minute, and 60- minute horizons, with ramp events constituting the highest change in future power output. We check robustness against autoregressive, LSTM, and GRU baselines plus several ensemble configurations, using Diebold-Mariano tests and bootstrap confidence intervals, and we vary the ramp threshold, compress the embeddings with PCA, and validate externally on Kaggle SCADA and NREL data with uncertainty-aware scoring. The semantic-context features produce negligible yet statistically significant gains over the baselines in multiple paired ensemble runs, most clearly at the 30- and 60-minute horizons where these gains hold across different ramp-threshold definitions, and PCA compression helps in some longer-horizon cases. The best context- augmented ensembles rank near the top overall, though the GRU model still posts the lowest ramp-event RMSE at 30 and 60 minutes. External tests confirm the error reduction generalizes across datasets, but the size of the gain depends on both model and dataset. Prediction intervals cover most test cases well but weaken during ramp events, pointing to a localized shift in the data distribution.

title: Neural Network-based Model for Detecting Credit Card Fraud: A Comparative Study of Oversampling Techniques and Feature Selection
abstract: Credit card fraud detection is complicated by the severe class imbalance typical of transaction data, because fraudulent cases represent only a small proportion of observations. This study develops a neural-network-based model for classifying transactions as legitimate or fraudulent and compares combinations of two oversampling techniques and two feature-selection approaches. The dataset contains 20,000 observations and 26 variables, with 339 fraudulent transactions (1.7%). After removing the transaction identifier and transforming categorical variables, class imbalance was addressed using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and Adaptive Synthetic Sampling (ADASYN). Relevant features were then selected using Pearson’s correlation coefficient or XGBoost, producing four configurations: SMOTE + Pearson, SMOTE + XGBoost, ADASYN + Pearson, and ADASYN + XGBoost. title: Hybrid CNN-RNN Architecture with MFCC-LFCC Features for Audio Deepfake Detection
abstract: The proliferation of sophisticated audio deepfake technology poses a significant threat to digital voice authentication and forensic verification systems. This research addresses this challenge by developing and evaluating a lightweight hybrid Convolutional Neural Network and Recurrent Neural Network (CNN-RNN) architecture for audio deepfake detection. The proposed model integrates a CNN for spatial feature extraction with a bidirectional RNN for temporal dependency modeling, utilizing an early vertically fused feature set of Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and Linear Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (LFCC) stabilized via utterance-level Cepstral Mean and Variance Normalization (CMVN). We assessed the proposed framework on the official ASVspoof 2019 Logical Access (LA) evaluation benchmark dataset (71,237 trials). Comprehensive evaluation on the official evaluation set demonstrated promising performance within the evaluated benchmark, achieving a Global Equal Error Rate (EER) of 8.24% and an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC-AUC) of 0.9680, while maintaining an internal validation EER of 0.33% on known attacks. While showing high sensitivity to bona fide speech and robust resilience against advanced Neural Text-to-Speech synthesis (EER < 0.25% for A07–A10), the framework exhibits notable vulnerability to phase-preserving voice conversion attacks. Consequently, without real-world forensic operational testing, the model serves as an initial diagnostic screening approach rather than a fully operational forensic solution, and still requires further cross-repository and noisy-condition validation.

title: Multimodal Intermediate-Task Training Effects on Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer in XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. title: BanglishChat: A Human vs. AI-Generated Banglish Chat Dataset for AI-Text and Impersonation-Scam Detection
abstract: This dataset supports research on detecting AI-generated text in Banglish (Bangla written using Latin/English characters), a code-mixed writing style widely used for everyday digital communication in Bangladesh. Motivation: fraudsters increasingly use AI chatbots (e.g., ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini, Grok) to impersonate friends, relatives, or institutional representatives in Banglish SMS/chat conversations to build trust, then extract money, credentials (OTP/PIN/passwords), or sensitive personal information from victims. Banglish is under-studied compared to standard Bangla or English, so existing AI-text-detection tools generalize poorly to it. This dataset supports building and evaluating classifiers that distinguish human-written from AI-generated Banglish text. Contents: 8,389 rows in a CSV with two columns — Human_chat (6,991 human-written Banglish messages) and AI_chat (7,976 AI-generated Banglish messages, produced by prompting ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini, and Grok to converse casually in Banglish). Full column definitions and summary statistics are provided in the accompanying DATA_DICTIONARY.md; usage notes and known limitations are in README.md. Intended use: training/evaluating human-vs-AI text classifiers for Banglish, code-mixed/low-resource NLP research, and research on impersonation-scam detection in South Asian digital communication. This dataset does not itself label messages as fraudulent; it labels only the authorship source (human or AI).

title: Quantum-Inspired Data Compression Based on Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to data compression leveraging principles inspired by quantum entanglement. Traditional classical data compression techniques are constrained by the linearity inherent in entropy calculations. We propose a methodology that seeks to generate correlations between data elements beyond the limitations imposed by classical entropy, mirroring the non-classical correlations observed in quantum entanglement. This exploration aims to achieve higher compression rates by introducing a fundamentally different approach to data representation. The core idea is to model the data as a system exhibiting entanglement-like properties, allowing for more efficient encoding. While full hardware implementation presents considerable challenges, this theoretical framework provides a new perspective on data compression, potentially unlocking significant improvements in compression ratios, particularly for data exhibiting complex correlations. The presented model utilizes a modified Shannon entropy formula incorporating correlation factors, denoted as *H(X,Y)*, where *X* and *Y* represent datasets. The core equation for compression is: *k = f(H(X,Y))* where *k* is the compression ratio and *f* is a function designed to exploit the correlations. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of "entanglement factors" (*Ei*) which quantify the degree of correlation between data elements. The overall compression process can be represented by: *Z = E1 * Z1 + E2 * Z2 + ... + EK * ZK*, where *Z* is the compressed data, *Zi* are the original data elements, and *Ei* are the entanglement factors. The success of this approach hinges on accurately estimating and modeling these entanglement factors.

title: Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing for Sparse Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to reservoir computing, termed Quantum-Inspired Reservoir Computing (QIRC), which aims to enhance the performance and efficiency of sparse neural networks by incorporating principles derived from quantum mechanics. Traditional reservoir computing relies on randomly generated, dense reservoirs, often leading to high computational costs and complex training procedures. QIRC addresses these challenges by designing a dynamically evolving, sparse reservoir exhibiting non-Markovian dynamics – a characteristic central to quantum systems. This reservoir is 'quantum-inspired', meaning it mimics the effects of superposition and entanglement without requiring actual quantum hardware. The core idea is to leverage these quantum-like properties to generate richer, more informative feature representations. We demonstrate that this approach can significantly reduce the training complexity of sparse neural networks, particularly for tasks involving complex, non-linear patterns. The paper details the design principles of the QIRC reservoir, its mathematical formulation, and the optimization techniques used to achieve superior performance compared to conventional reservoir computing methods. We present a theoretical framework that connects the dynamics of the QIRC reservoir to the concepts of quantum superposition and entanglement, providing a justification for the observed improvements. Finally, we outline future research directions, including exploring different reservoir dynamics and investigating the potential for QIRC in various applications.

title: Adaptive Data Sampling Algorithm Based on Information Gain
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive data sampling algorithm designed to enhance sampling efficiency and accuracy. The core of the algorithm lies in leveraging information gain theory to dynamically adjust sampling probabilities based on the inherent characteristics of the data. Unlike traditional sampling methods that often employ fixed or rule-based strategies, this approach provides a more intelligent and responsive solution. The algorithm iteratively assesses the information value of each data sample and updates the sampling probability accordingly. This dynamic adaptation allows the algorithm to prioritize sampling from regions of the data space with higher uncertainty or potential for significant information gain. This research addresses the limitations of static sampling approaches and offers a novel method for optimizing data sampling in various applications, including machine learning, data mining, and anomaly detection. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, paving the way for future experimental validation.

title: Dimensional Multi-Aspect Quantum Error Correction Protocol
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum information processing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum states. Traditional QEC protocols often rely on a fixed number of dimensions, limiting their effectiveness in addressing complex quantum systems exhibiting intricate error patterns. This paper introduces a novel Dimensional Multi-Aspect (DMA) quantum error correction protocol, leveraging the principles of non-standard quantum error correction and dynamically adjusting the quantum state's dimensionality to precisely rectify quantum state distortions caused by varying dimensional differences. We demonstrate the protocol's effectiveness in mitigating specific error patterns and highlighting its potential to overcome the limitations of traditional QEC. The core mechanism involves a dynamic "dimensional jump" process, carefully orchestrated to exploit quantum error correction properties. This innovation promises a significant advancement in the robustness and accuracy of quantum information processing.

title: Adaptive Kernel Methods with Neural Network Feature Extraction
abstract: Kernel methods have demonstrated remarkable success in various machine learning tasks, particularly in scenarios involving high-dimensional data. However, their computational cost, often scaling quadratically or worse with the number of data points, can be a significant bottleneck, particularly when dealing with large datasets. This paper proposes a novel approach to adaptive kernel learning by integrating neural networks for dynamic feature extraction. The core idea is to leverage a neural network to learn a feature representation of the data, and subsequently define a kernel function based on these learned features. This adaptive process allows the kernel method to dynamically adjust to the underlying data distribution, potentially mitigating the computational challenges associated with traditional kernel methods while improving performance. The method is presented with a theoretical framework and the core claim is that Kernel methods can be computationally expensive for large datasets. This approach integrates neural networks to dynamically learn kernel functions. The mechanism is that A neural network learns to extract features from the data, and a kernel function is defined based on these learned features, adapting to the data distribution. This approach is new because it dynamically learns kernel functions using neural networks, potentially reducing computational complexity and improving performance.

title: Title: Adaptive Neural Networks for Complex Data Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network modeling, focusing on adaptive neural networks designed to effectively capture complex data patterns. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts network structure and parameters based on data feature variations, thereby enhancing model performance. The core claim of this work is that a specifically designed adaptive neural network offers superior data modeling capabilities compared to existing methods. This research addresses the limitations of conventional neural networks by emphasizing data-driven adaptation, leading to improved generalization and robustness. The study explores the integration of a novel self-adaptive network structure with a feedback mechanism to optimize model parameters in response to data characteristics. The resulting network architecture demonstrates enhanced performance on a suite of benchmark datasets, validating the proposed approach's efficacy in complex data modeling.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Adaptive Computation: A Novel Approach to Complex Problem Solving
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre and fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a potential pathway to revolutionary computing capabilities. This paper explores the concept of "Quantum Entanglement-Driven Adaptive Computation" (QEDAC), a novel computational paradigm leveraging the unique properties of entangled quantum states. We propose a mechanism where quantum computations are dynamically adjusted based on environmental factors, offering a potential solution to problems intractable for classical computers. This work emphasizes the critical role of quantum entanglement in enabling adaptive computation, addressing limitations of existing approaches and highlighting a promising direction for future quantum research. The core claim is that QEDAC can significantly enhance the adaptability and problem-solving potential of quantum computers.

title: WildfireSpreadBench: The Metric Decides the Model in Wildfire Spread Prediction
abstract: Machine learning is being increasingly used to predict where active wildfires will burn the following day, helping inform evacuation boundaries and containment lines. Most models are evaluated using Average Precision (AP), which summarizes performance across all decision thresholds, although acting on a forecast requires choosing one. We benchmarked five discriminative architectures and one generative model on WildfireSpreadTS using a shared evaluation pipeline and two input configurations. We found that model rankings varied depending on whether performance was measured by AP or by threshold-dependent metrics like F1 and IoU. At the default 0.5 threshold, the highest-AP model flagged 4 to 5 times the observed active-fire area and ranked fifth of six on F1 and IoU, and the most recall-heavy model flagged 16 to 23 times. The three models whose flagged area stayed close to the observed area had AP scores 24 to 37% lower. Across models, we identified three distinct prediction profiles: over-predicting, balanced, and under-predicting, which AP alone could not distinguish. Expanding the input from 7 to 23 channels changed AP by 0.03 on average, against a 0.21 to 0.24 spread across models. Ultimately, these results show that AP alone can favor models whose predictions are poorly suited for operational wildfire forecasting.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Anti-UAV Detection via Evidential Fusion and Conflict-Discounted Belief Aggregation
abstract: Anti-UAV perception systems must remain reliable when sensor streams degrade under occlusion, fast motion, or modality-specific failure. Existing multimodal anti-UAV systems fuse RGB and thermal streams deterministically, without modeling predictive uncertainty, and cannot express doubt when streams disagree. Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) produces calibrated per-class uncertainty in a single forward pass. EDTC already exploits this for thermal-only perception, yet cross-modal evidential fusion remains unaddressed. This paper extends EDTC to multimodal RGB-Thermal perception via Discounted Belief Fusion (DBF), which converts inter-modal conflict into uncertainty mass before aggregating stream opinions. Bounding boxes are resolved by selecting the lower-uncertainty modality. On the Anti-UAV benchmark, multimodal fusion consistently outperforms either single stream (test Acc 0.670 vs. 0.604 IR, 0.598 RGB) at real-time speed (at least 38 FPS). However, DBF is empirically indistinguishable from undiscounted averaging: near-zero inter-modal conflict on this presence-dominated benchmark leaves the discounting step inert. The fused uncertainty is well-calibrated (ECE 0.057) yet expectedly a weaker localization failure detector than spatial variance (AUROC 0.626 vs. 0.739). The null result is structural: the benchmark's near-universal presence and vacuous miss-encoding jointly suppress inter-modal conflict, a diagnosis that delimits where conflict-aware fusion provides measurable benefit.

title: WoE Wrote It? Watermarking Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Black-Box Text Provenance
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) watermarks provide a mechanism for text provenance, enabling model owners to identify machine-generated content and attribute it to a specific watermarked model. However, current LLM watermarking approaches predominantly rely on inference-time sampler methods and focus their analysis on dense models. Inference-time methods are only effective when the text is explicitly generated via the model owner's controlled API; they fail in a post-compromise scenario. An adversary who steals or leaks the model weights gains complete control over inference and can simply run an unmodified sampler, bypassing the watermark and preventing post-theft attribution. In this work, we introduce Watermarking of Experts (WoE), a novel black-box text provenance method that leverages the unique structural properties of sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. WoE biases the vocabulary of specific experts and shifts the watermark signal embedding away from unenforceable inference wrappers. This approach ensures the watermark remains intrinsic to the model parameters, enabling defenders to attribute text generated by stolen weights, leaked checkpoints, and secondary dense models distilled from the stolen architecture without needing access to the adversary's deployment or weights. We evaluate WoE across eight MoE models, demonstrating successful watermark detection from suspect text, achieving an average true positive rate of 90.1% at a 1% false positive rate, reaching up to 94.9%, while largely preserving general model utility. Furthermore, WoE remains detectable under adversarial supervised fine-tuning, model extraction, and output-level paraphrasing, forcing malicious actors into a trade-off in which weakening the attribution signal requires additional model adaptation or text-rewriting operations, or compromises the utility of the resulting output.
