title: 基于语义拓扑的动态程序优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to dynamic program optimization based on semantic topology. The core idea is to represent program code and data structures as semantic topology graphs, enabling a more intelligent and adaptive optimization process compared to traditional static optimization techniques. The method utilizes formal semantic analysis to construct these graphs, capturing dependencies between code elements. Subsequently, graph algorithms and heuristic algorithms are employed to identify optimization opportunities within the graph, dynamically adapting to the program's execution behavior. This approach addresses the limitations of static optimization by providing a 'perceptual' and 'adaptive' system capable of effectively handling complex dependencies and generating optimized strategies. The system's dynamic nature stems from the real-time updating of the semantic topology graph, reflecting changes in the program's semantics during execution. Key contributions include the formulation of program optimization as a graph-based problem and the integration of dynamic semantic topology for enhanced optimization.

title: Hybrid Machine Learning Model for Credit Card Fraud Detection Using SVM, Decision Tree, and Naive Bayes
abstract: Credit card fraud is a major challenge in digital financial transactions due to the increasing use of online payments and electronic banking. Traditional fraud detection methods face difficulties in identifying evolving fraudulent patterns while minimizing false alarms. This paper proposes a hybrid machine learning model combining Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), and Naive Bayes (NB) using an Adaptive Weighted Voting mechanism. The Credit Card Fraud Detection Dataset is preprocessed using feature standardization and Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to address class imbalance. The three classifiers are trained independently and their predictions are combined using validation-based weights. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves 99.08% accuracy, 98.72% precision, 98.15% recall, 98.43% F1-score, and 99.41% ROC-AUC, outperforming the individual classifiers. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of adaptive ensemble learning for reliable credit card fraud detection.

title: Vocabulary Growth Fundamentals: Bernstein Functions and Hausdorff Sequences
abstract: We survey the theory of vocabulary growth founded in the setting of stochastic processes. In particular, we model the expected number of types through Bernstein functions and Hausdorff sequences. These classes of mathematical objects, defined by alternating signs of their derivatives or differences, can be related to continuous-time Poisson point processes and discrete-time IID processes, respectively. Building on previous accounts of the vocabulary growth, we integrate the broader theories of Bernstein functions and Hausdorff sequences and connect them with recently developed hapax rate models. In particular, we prove that the logistic hapax rate model has a non-negative spectrum and hence it defines a Bernstein function, thereby solving an earlier posed problem. We also analyze the limitations of the Bernstein--Hausdorff theory of the vocabulary growth by considering its generalizations under stationary and Weibull renewal processes.

title: Localizing Emergent Failures in Agentic AI: Recovering Minimal Repair Families via Counterfactual Replay
abstract: Failures in agentic AI systems can arise from interactions among messages exchanged by multiple large language model (LLM) agents. Pointwise attribution cannot distinguish a jointly necessary repair from alternative singleton repairs. We formulate Minimal Repair Family Recovery (MRFR): recovering all inclusion-minimal event sets whose counterfactual replay restores task success within a declared size bound. We propose Graph-Constrained Joint Replay (GCJR), which slices failure-relevant events from an execution dependency graph, constructs graph-feasible singleton and pair candidates, and verifies them by replay with paired clean counterparts. For fixed replay outcomes, GCJR is exact within its declared graph domain. title: Multi-Step Forecasting of Grape Berry Temperature based on LSTM Model with Feed-Forward Attention
abstract: Accurate forecasting of grape berry temperature (Tb) is essential for enabling timely heat stress management in vineyards. In this study, a feed-forward attention mechanism integrated with a Long Short-Term Memory network (FAM-LSTM) was developed and evaluated for multi-step, high-resolution Tb prediction. Models were trained using environmental data from 2023 and 2024 at Prosser, WA, USA, and validated on 2025 summer data. FAM-LSTM was benchmarked against LSTM, GRU, RNN, and Random Forest (RF) across horizons ranging from 15 minutes to 72 hours (288 time steps). Two input scenarios were evaluated: nearest open-field weather station observations and in-vineyard microclimate measurements. FAM-LSTM consistently outperformed all benchmark models across all horizons and input scenarios. Incorporating in-vineyard microclimate data significantly improved forecasting accuracy at longer horizons. Using open-field data, FAM-LSTM achieved MAE and RMSE ranges of 0.58 to 1.70 deg C and 0.65 to 2.07 deg C, respectively. In-vineyard observations further improved performance, with MAE and RMSE in the ranges of 0.51 to 1.55 deg C and 0.71 to 1.87 deg C. Error analysis showed prediction uncertainty was highest during peak daytime periods (11:00 to 18:00) and increased progressively with forecast horizon. Overall, the FAM-LSTM framework offers robust Tb forecasting to support precision heat stress management in vineyards.

title: Generative AI for Plain Language: A Comparative Study of Prompt Strategies and Linguists Validation.
abstract: The technical complexity and “legalese” inherent in official documents create significant cognitive barriers that reduce public transparency and hinder the effective exercise of digital citizenship. While manual plain language and Natural Language Processing (NLP) initiatives exist in the public sector to mitigate these problems, scaling these efforts to handle massive volumes of text remains a significant challenge, highlighting the need for automated solutions. In this context, the main objective of this study is to evaluate the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) as a tool for rewriting official documents according to plain language guidelines. We generated 18 versions of six document typologies using GPT-4o-mini, comparing zero-shot, one-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting. The evaluation employed a hybrid approach: qualitative assessment by expert linguists alongside statistical readability (Flesch-Kincaid) and semantic similarity metrics (BERTScore, BLEU). Additionally, the “LLM-as-a-judge” pipeline was implemented to test automated reviewing. Results show that while GenAI consistently improves readability to high-school levels, no single prompt strategy is universally optimal, and its effectiveness heavily depends on the document’s structure. Furthermore, the LLM-as-a-judge experiment failed to replicate human judgment, showing low correlation with experts. We conclude that adopting LLMs in the public sector demands “Human-in-the-loop” workflows to ensure legal accuracy and clear communication.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference in Complex Networks
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference aims to improve the accuracy and speed of inference in complex networks by incorporating quantum principles. This paper explores the potential of quantum annealing and superposition to address limitations of existing algorithms, particularly in handling high-dimensional and intricate network structures. We present a novel algorithm that leverages these quantum mechanics concepts to enhance probabilistic representation and lead to more reliable inference results. The core claim is that quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference offers significant advancements over classical methods, particularly for large-scale complex networks.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Graph Theory for Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a profound challenge for robust data storage and secure communication. Traditional entanglement models, while effective, often struggle with maintaining entanglement across multiple qubits, particularly in the presence of noise and decoherence. This paper explores the application of non-Euclidean graph theory principles to this challenge, proposing a novel framework for understanding and manipulating quantum entanglement. We formalize and extend graph theory concepts – specifically graph coloring and modularity – to the quantum state space, developing a new language for describing and controlling entanglement. Our analysis reveals the potential for this approach to offer a more robust and flexible framework, potentially leading to enhanced quantum algorithms and security protocols. This work addresses a fundamental gap in our understanding of entanglement and opens new avenues for research in quantum information theory.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization for Neural Network Training
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization offers a promising approach to accelerate and stabilize neural network training, addressing the limitations of classical optimization methods. This paper explores the implementation of a novel quantum-inspired technique, incorporating quantum annealing and enhanced gradient descent, to enhance the learning process and mitigate overfitting. We provide a detailed examination of the theoretical underpinnings, experimental results, and potential applications of this approach. The core claim centers around achieving significant improvements in training speed and model robustness compared to traditional optimization methods. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's effectiveness, highlighting its advantages and limitations.

title: Dynamic Semantic Dependency Graph Reasoning (DSDT-Reasoning)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Semantic Dependency Graph Reasoning (DSDT-Reasoning), a novel approach to program analysis and optimization that leverages machine learning to dynamically understand and reason about semantic dependencies within program execution. The core claim is that by constructing and continuously updating a machine learning-based semantic dependency graph, the system can overcome the limitations of static type systems and traditional dependency analysis techniques, enabling finer-grained optimizations and more accurate error detection. The system monitors abstract execution representations, feeding data into a multi-layered neural network architecture that learns to identify semantic dependencies such as read/write dependencies between variables, function call dependencies, and memory access dependencies. The generated dependency graph is dynamically updated to reflect the program's actual state. This dynamic graph facilitates optimizations like dead code elimination and memory allocation optimization, and supports precise error detection, including data races, memory leaks, and type errors. DSDT-Reasoning represents a significant advancement over static analysis methods reliant on static information and predefined rules, and surpasses simple dependency graph construction by utilizing deep learning for semantic understanding and inference.

title: Quantum Entanglement for Non-linear Adaptive Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds the potential for revolutionary computing capabilities. This paper investigates the application of quantum entanglement to non-linear adaptive computation, proposing a novel approach leveraging the inherent self-associativity of entangled states. We present a design for a quantum computation algorithm utilizing entangled qubits to achieve enhanced precision compared to conventional methods. The core mechanism centers on dynamically adjusting the entangled state to optimize the computation's output. This work explores the potential of entanglement to overcome limitations in current computing paradigms, specifically focusing on the design of a method exhibiting high accuracy through self-associativity. The study highlights the promise of this approach for tackling complex problems requiring high precision.

title: Program Synthesis and Formal Verification: A Collaborative Approach
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to software verification by synergistically combining program synthesis and formal verification techniques. The core idea is to establish a collaborative workflow where a program synthesizer generates candidate program code, and a formal verification tool automatically assesses its correctness. The feedback loop enables iterative refinement and optimization of the synthesized code, dramatically increasing both the reliability and efficiency of the program synthesis process. This approach minimizes the need for extensive human intervention, offering a pathway toward fully automated software development and verification. We outline the key components of this framework, discuss the challenges involved, and present a conceptual model for its implementation. The proposed methodology represents a significant step towards achieving robust and trustworthy software systems.

title: Bio-Inspired Algorithms for Representation Learning of Massive Datasets
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to representation learning for massive datasets, inspired by the self-organizing principles observed in biological neural networks. Traditional deep learning methods often struggle with the computational demands of extremely large datasets, leading to scalability issues and potential performance bottlenecks. Our approach leverages the inherent efficiency and adaptability of biological systems by mimicking the self-organizing mechanisms found in neural networks. Specifically, we construct a framework that replicates key aspects of neural connectivity and activation functions, resulting in a highly scalable and effective representation learning system. The core claim is that simulating the self-organization of biological neural networks can efficiently learn representations from massive datasets. The central mechanism involves modeling the dynamic connections and activation patterns within a network, allowing for the extraction of salient features and the creation of compact, informative representations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, outlining a scalable architecture that addresses the limitations of current methods. The proposed framework offers a promising alternative for tackling the representation learning challenges posed by the ever-increasing volume of data in various domains. ---

title: Based on Multi-Qubit Topological Quantum Error Correction for Quantum Cloud Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing multi-qubit topological quantum error correction (TQEC) to construct a robust quantum cloud computing platform. The core concept centers on leveraging the inherent resilience of topological qubits against local environmental noise through TQEC protocols, enabling the reliable sharing and utilization of quantum computing resources. We detail the synergistic combination of topological quantum computation and quantum error correction, outlining a framework for delivering quantum computing services. The novelty lies in directly applying these advanced techniques to the quantum cloud computing paradigm, facilitating scalable and dependable quantum computation access. This approach addresses a critical bottleneck in the development of quantum computing – the challenge of maintaining qubit coherence – while simultaneously unlocking the potential for widespread quantum application development and deployment. The proposed architecture incorporates sophisticated decoding algorithms and resource management strategies to maximize the efficiency and reliability of the cloud platform. We present a theoretical framework demonstrating the feasibility and potential advantages of this system, focusing on key aspects such as error rates, qubit connectivity, and the scalability of the error correction process. ---

title: Enhancing DES Encryption Efficiency through a Metrics-Centric Pipeline and AI-Driven Analytical Framework
abstract: This paper introduces an improved Data Encryption Standard (DES) framework that incorporates a metrics-driven data processing pipeline, AI-powered analytical decision support and a quantum-inspired entropy-based key generation process to enhance both encryption efficiency and key security. It validates data, preprocesses it, encodes it, optimizes it, encrypts it, monitors it in real-time, analyzes entropy and also analyzes the execution time, encryption speed, throughput, CPU utilization, memory consumption and key randomness. Experimental results indicate that the encryption throughput was achieved on average at 5.11 MB/s, with a maximum value of 12.15 MB/s, while the time required for encryption and decryption were on average 42.67 ms and 44.21 ms, respectively. The proposed quantum-inspired key generator has an average key entropy of 0.82 (compared with 0.68 for standard random keys) and a higher uniformity of 0.88 (compared with 0.72 for standard random keys), which corresponds to an approximately 20.6% improvement. Furthermore, the quantum-inspired approach achieved a maximum entropy of 0.95 compared with 0.89 for random generation, and its strongest keys had a collision rate of no more than 0.01%. The overall average security improvement for the AI analysis was 13.30% and the overall completion rate for the full processing pipeline was 98.50%. The findings highlight practical solutions for optimizing the performance, randomness, and security evaluation of DES-based encryption by incorporating AI-driven analysis, entropy-driven key generation, and regular monitoring.

title: Binturong Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Bio-inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm based on Canopy Exploration and Scent-guided Precision Foraging
abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms have been widely used in science and engineering due to their ability to solve complex optimization problems, but striking an effective balance between exploration and exploitation remains one of the most important challenges in this field.In this study, Binturong Optimization Algorithm (BOA) is introduced as a new population-based metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the natural behaviors of Binturong.First, the biological behaviors of this animal are analyzed, and then BOA is modeled in three stages including initialization, exploration phase, and exploitation phase.exploration phase is designed based on Canopy Exploration behavior to extensively explore the search space and maintain population diversity, while exploitation phase is developed inspired by Scent-Guided Precision Foraging behavior to perform precise local search and improve promising solutions.The performance of BOA is evaluated using a comprehensive set of simulation studies.First, the search behavior of the algorithm is analyzed from the perspective of population diversity and exploration-exploitation dynamics.The results show that BOA strikes a good balance between exploration and exploitation during the optimization process and provides a stable and efficient search process.Then, the performance of the algorithm on unimodal test functions (F1-F7), high-dimensional multimodal test functions (F8-F13) and fixed-dimensional multimodal test functions (F14-F23) is investigated and compared with 9 well-known metaheuristic algorithms.The simulation results show that BOA ranks first in all 23 benchmark functions and, as a result, has achieved a 100% success rate compared to competing algorithms.These findings indicate that BOA, with its high ability to strike a balance between exploration and exploitation, is a powerful, stable and competitive optimizer and can be used in a wide range of optimization problems, various sciences and real-world applications.

title: The State of the Art in Satellite Quantum Key Distribution: Protocols, Technologies, and Physical Limits
abstract: ABSTRACT This review presents the state of the art in quantum key distribution (QKD) for satellite‐to‐ground free‐space optical links. It first surveys continuous‐variable, discrete‐variable, entanglement‐based, measurement‐device‐independent, and twin‐field protocols, and discusses their feasibility under the losses and time‐varying conditions of orbital passes. It also distinguishes protocol security from practical implementation security. The paper then reviews enabling technologies, including single‐photon sources and detectors, followed by atmospheric impairments, time‐evolving turbulence, aperture averaging, and adaptive optics. Finally, physical channel limits and the trust assumptions of satellite‐network architectures are discussed. Overall, the literature indicates that discrete‐variable decoy‐state BB84 in LEO downlink configurations is the most mature near‐term SatQKD option, including for daylight operation when appropriate filtering and pointing/turbulence mitigation are employed.

title: SS-ESOAP: Self-Scaled Adaptive Preconditioning for Physics-Informed Learning
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often face ill-conditioned objectives that limit high-accuracy training. Dense quasi-Newton methods improve local conditioning but require expensive optimizer state, while Kronecker-factored methods such as SOAP scale to larger networks but rely on periodic basis updates. We introduce \method, which augments SOAP-style preconditioning with a scalar secant-energy correction adapted to Kronecker geometry and an adaptive basis update followed by variance-state downscaling. We characterize the directional secant matching induced by the scalar correction and give a bound on variance-state mismatch across basis changes. Across eight PDE benchmarks, \method attains the lowest final residual on six, including Burgers and Boussinesq, while SOAP-family baselines perform better on Gray-Scott and Ginzburg-Landau. On Boussinesq, \method reaches a residual of $10^{-5}$ in 4.1 hours with 9.2 GB peak VRAM, while Adam does not reach this target within 14 hours. Three-seed $L^2$ and $H^1$ errors on four representative PDEs support the link between lower residuals and improved solution accuracy. These results position \method as a scalable option for stiff, high-accuracy physics-informed training, rather than a uniform replacement for existing optimizers.

title: Using Channel Representations in Regularization Terms: A Case Study on Image Diffusion
abstract: In this work we propose a novel non-linear diffusion filtering approach for images based on their channel representation. To derive the diffusion update scheme we formulate a novel energy functional using a soft-histogram representation of image pixel neighborhoods obtained from the channel encoding. The resulting Euler-Lagrange equation yields a non-linear robust diffusion scheme with additional weighting terms stemming from the channel representation which steer the diffusion process. We apply this novel energy formulation to image reconstruction problems, showing good performance in the presence of mixtures of Gaussian and impulse-like noise, e.g. missing data. In denoising experiments of common scalar-valued images our approach performs competitive compared to other diffusion schemes as well as state-of-the-art denoising methods for the considered noise types.

The resulting Euler-Lagrange equation yields a non-linear robust diffusion scheme with additional weighting terms stemming from the channel representation which steer the diffusion process. We apply this novel energy formulation to image reconstruction problems, showing good performance in the presence of mixtures of Gaussian and impulse-like noise, e.g. missing data. In denoising experiments of common scalar-valued images our approach performs competitive compared to other diffusion schemes as well as state-of-the-art denoising methods for the considered noise types.

title: Eigenvalues of multipartite entanglement witnesses
abstract: We investigate various properties of multipartite block-positive operators, decomposable EWs (DEWs), and non-decomposable EWs. We provide a necessary and sufficient condition to construct a special DEW using the multipartite GHZ state. For multipartite DEW, we explicitly characterize the supremum and infimum of maximum and minimum eigenvalues, as well as the trace of its square. We also derive other results concerning NDEW, eigenvalues of $2 \times n$ EWs and the corresponding physical implications. Furthermore, we investigate the tightness of inequalities of these eigenvalues with examples.

title: Graph Representation Learning with Dynamic Attention Mechanisms
abstract: This paper investigates the limitations of static attention mechanisms within graph representation learning and proposes a novel approach utilizing dynamic attention mechanisms. Static attention models, prevalent in graph representation learning, struggle to effectively capture the evolving and complex relationships inherent in graph data. Our method introduces a dynamic attention framework where attention weights are learned and continuously updated based on the changing interactions between nodes. This allows the model to adapt to shifts in relationships, leading to improved performance in downstream graph tasks. The core claim is that static attention mechanisms limit the ability to capture dynamic relationships, and the proposed model directly addresses this limitation. The key mechanism involves the dynamic adjustment of attention weights, providing a more nuanced and accurate representation of graph structures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual overview, highlighting its potential for advancing graph representation learning.

title: 基于动态量子拓扑的机器学习模型设计
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic quantum topology learning to machine learning, aiming to enhance model generalization capabilities. Traditional machine learning often relies on fixed features, limiting the model's ability to capture complex relationships within data. We propose a novel methodology leveraging quantum topology, specifically a dynamic quantum topology learning algorithm, to represent data through the evolution of quantum states. This approach allows for a more nuanced and adaptive learning process, potentially unlocking improved predictive performance compared to conventional methods. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing quantum state dynamics to automatically extract and represent relevant features, thereby fostering a more robust and generalizable model. The paper details the proposed algorithm, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential for enhancing machine learning models.

title: Homomorphic Encryption-Based Distributed Database Querying
abstract: This paper proposes a novel system for distributed database querying that leverages the power of homomorphic encryption (HE) and differential privacy (DP) to provide secure and privacy-preserving query capabilities. The core idea is to perform all query operations on encrypted data without ever decrypting the underlying database records. This is achieved by mapping the query operations to encrypted mathematical functions and utilizing the inherent properties of HE to execute them directly on the encrypted data. Differential privacy is integrated to mitigate the risk of information leakage from the query results, adding an extra layer of protection. The system architecture is designed for scalability and efficiency, allowing for complex queries to be executed across multiple database nodes. The proposed approach addresses the significant privacy concerns associated with traditional distributed database querying systems, offering a viable solution for applications requiring secure data analysis and reporting. The system is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential to provide strong privacy guarantees while maintaining query functionality. The key contributions of this work lie in the combined utilization of HE and DP for distributed database querying, offering a novel paradigm for secure data access.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Quantum Circuit Design
abstract: The design of optimal quantum circuits for specific tasks remains a significant challenge due to the exponentially growing complexity of possible circuit architectures. Traditional optimization methods struggle to navigate this vast design space effectively. This work proposes a novel approach leveraging probabilistic programming languages and Bayesian optimization to address this problem. We represent quantum circuits as probabilistic programs and utilize Bayesian optimization to efficiently explore the design space, driven by objective functions that quantify desired circuit properties such as fidelity and gate count. This approach allows for a systematic and data-driven exploration, moving beyond exhaustive search methods. The core contribution lies in the application of probabilistic programming to quantum circuit design, offering a scalable and adaptive framework for discovering high-performance circuits. The methodology presented provides a framework for efficient exploration of quantum circuit design space, which is critical for realizing the potential of quantum computing.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Monte Carlo Tree Search for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) algorithms, a cornerstone technique in reinforcement learning and game AI. The core claim is that by harnessing quantum superposition and interference, we can significantly accelerate MCTS's exploration of complex optimization landscapes. The proposed approach utilizes quantum circuits to represent and evaluate game states, leveraging quantum parallelism to concurrently assess multiple branches of the search tree. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and algorithmic design, how this quantum-enhanced MCTS can outperform classical MCTS in scenarios with high computational complexity and vast search spaces. The resulting system offers a novel approach to solving complex optimization problems, particularly those found in areas such as game playing, portfolio optimization, and drug discovery. The presented methodology focuses on the conceptual framework and provides a roadmap for future research and development, emphasizing the integration of quantum hardware with sophisticated reinforcement learning strategies. The key innovation lies in the efficient mapping of the MCTS search process onto a quantum computing architecture, exploiting quantum mechanics to dramatically reduce the search time.

title: Distributed Machine Learning Based on Multivariate Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement in distributed machine learning (DML) to address the challenges of data sharing and model merging across multiple nodes. Traditional DML systems often suffer from significant communication overhead and computational bottlenecks due to the need for centralized data storage and model aggregation. We propose a novel framework leveraging multivariate entanglement to facilitate efficient data sharing and model consolidation. The core concept involves entangling the input data streams of multiple learning nodes. This entanglement allows for correlated data access and enables a distributed model merging process that minimizes communication costs and computational complexity. This approach offers the potential to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of DML systems compared to conventional methods. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key equations and mathematical models employed to demonstrate the feasibility and performance of the proposed approach. We define key terms and concepts, focusing on the entanglement entropy, correlation coefficients, and the overall performance metrics used to evaluate the effectiveness of the distributed learning system. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of this technology.

title: ##混沌控制的非结构化优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-structured optimization algorithm based on chaos control. Traditional optimization methods rely on predefined objectives, limiting their flexibility. Our algorithm leverages the inherent self-organization properties of chaotic systems to learn and generate optimization paths from seemingly random or disordered data. The core mechanism involves simulating the system's dynamics to develop a robust and adaptive optimization strategy. The proposed algorithm demonstrates superior performance in a range of optimization tasks, showcasing its potential to overcome the limitations of conventional approaches. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation, highlighting its key advantages and potential applications.

title: Digital Voter Behavior: A Text Mining Approach to Analyzing Political Party Perceptions on X
abstract: Social media provides an important source for analyzing public opinion and societal trends. This study examines sentiment toward five political parties in Türkiye using sentiment analysis of Turkish tweets. More than 60,000 tweets collected via the X API on May 11, 12, and 14, 2023, were used to select a balanced dataset of 1,250 tweets, with 250 tweets per party. Tweets were classified as positive, neutral, or negative and analyzed using Naive Bayes and Decision Tree algorithms. The results indicate similar classification performance between the two algorithms, while sentiment distributions varied across political parties and sentiment categories. The study contributes to research on the relationship between social media and politics by demonstrating the potential of sentiment analysis for evaluating political discourse.

title: Whose Assessment of Distress? Community Perspectives and LLM Alignment on Well-Being Posts
abstract: Judgments about psychological distress are socially situated: what counts as concerning hinges on community norms around emotional expression, vulnerability, and help-seeking. Yet large language models (LLMs) used for distress detection are typically aligned to a single, undifferentiated standard. How well do these models capture the perspectives of the communities whose language they assess? We address this question through a perspectivist annotation study in which 321 participants provided 9,587 judgments on 1,198 Reddit posts spanning six identity-based communities, yielding community-specific labels. Raters in the contextualized in-group condition show a modest tendency to agree more with their community than uncontextualized out-group raters (OR = 1.18), an effect varying significantly across communities. We then evaluate nine open-weight LLM configurations and four frontier configurations against these labels. Open-weight LLMs systematically over-estimate distress: when communities perceive none-to-mild distress, these models achieve only 31-44% accuracy, predominantly producing false positives. GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro show the same none-to-mild inflation even when their full-sample over/under rates are mixed, while Claude Opus 4 is more conservative. This pattern does not simply mirror an outsider reading position: uncontextualized out-group human aggregates were nearly symmetric, with 18% over-estimation versus 19% under-estimation. Instead, the models that inflate none-to-mild cases exhibit a distress prior that exceeds both contextualized in-group and uncontextualized out-group human judgments. These findings have implications for equitable AI deployment in mental health contexts, where miscalibrated distress detection may unevenly affect the communities being assessed.

title: On systematicity of linear function-correcting codes
abstract: The standard formulation of function-correcting codes uses systematic encodings. We study the redundancy cost of this constraint when both the prescribed function and the encoding are linear. We introduce the function-separation distance and show that several classical unequal error protection parameters are special cases. For linear functions and encodings, this distance is the first relative generalized Hamming weight of the code relative to the encoded kernel. We formulate free and systematic linear separation problems. We prove that the optimal free redundancy depends only on the rank of the function, and determine the optimal systematic redundancy for prescribed separations $d\leq3$.

title: Computational Depth Measurement in Thermographic Video: Overcoming Spatial Overfitting via Spatio-Temporal Decoupling
abstract: Accurate through-thickness measurement of subsurface delamination depth in Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) is important for structural assessment because defect location determines affected load-bearing layers. Optical pulsed thermography (OPT) provides a two-dimensional thermal video rather than volumetric measurements, so depth must be inferred from temporal heat-diffusion responses. A challenge is spatial dataset bias: when calibration defects follow regular grids, regression models may memorize their geometry instead of learning physical relationship between thermal decay and depth. This work introduces a spatio-temporal decoupling architecture that separates spatial defect localization from temporal depth measurement. Defect regions are first localized using segmentation methods, after which thermal responses are spatially averaged and converted into sixteen physics-informed temporal, energy, statistical, and geometric features. These features expose the one-dimensional heat-conduction relationship while withholding pixel coordinates from the depth model. Four regression models are evaluated using specimen-level cross-validation: Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), Advanced Multi-Layer Perceptron (Adv-MLP), and XGBoost. Unregularized trees and over-parameterized Adv-MLP exhibit calibration collapse under geometric shifts, with errors exceeding 0.5 mm. In contrast, regularized XGBoost with L1/L2 penalties and column sampling maintains cross-specimen calibration, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.056 mm and root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.085 mm. Predicted depths are merged with masks to generate Delaunay-triangulated three-dimensional defect models in three to five seconds per specimen. Results show that mathematical regularization and spatio-temporal decoupling reduce spatial memorization in thermal-video depth regression.

title: RoSe-SLAM: Robust Semantic-Aware Gaussian Splatting SLAM from Dynamic Monocular Videos
abstract: In dynamic and unstructured environments, conventional SLAM systems generally suffer from significant accuracy degeneration due to their static assumptions. In this work, we propose Robust Semantic-aware Gaussian Splatting SLAM (RoSe-SLAM), to address the dynamic challenge by a holistic semantic scene understanding from uncalibrated monocular inputs, achieving accurate camera tracking and high-quality geometry reconstruction. Unlike conventional semantic SLAM using handcrafted semantic labels, our RoSe-SLAM exploits the semantic feature from 2D foundation model to enhance the dynamic tracking and mapping performance. By distilling the rich semantic features to our Gaussian fields, our method effectively identifies dynamic distractors and achieves semantic-aware multi-view consistency, significantly enhancing the geometric reconstruction and scene inpainting. Specifically, we propose a spatial-temporal motion mask generation module, enabling both long-term motion monitoring and short-term transient dynamics capturing, achieving robust and effective disentanglement of dynamic objects and static backgrounds. During global bundle adjustment, we propose an occlusion-aware keyframe selection mechanism to prioritize the occlusion as metric to pick the keyframes, and a multi-view semantic consistency module to improve the mapping quality in dynamic environments. By combining geometric motion cues with semantic priors, our system dynamically filters unreliable observations and reconstructs accurate static scene geometry. Extensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets including dynamic TUM, Bonn and Wild-Mocap datasets, demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance in both trajectory estimation and static scene mapping, outperforming existing dynamic RGB SLAM baselines in long-term dynamic indoor environments.

title: Quantum State Space Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state space learning algorithm designed to enhance the efficiency of quantum systems through optimized parameter adjustment. Traditional approaches primarily rely on classical parameter tuning, limiting the potential for significant performance gains. This algorithm leverages the inherent properties of quantum state spaces—specifically, quantum entanglement and superposition—to dynamically learn and refine quantum system parameters, offering a fundamentally different approach to optimization. The core mechanism centers around constructing and manipulating a quantum state space representation to effectively guide the system towards optimal performance. This advancement holds significant promise for accelerating quantum computation and expanding the capabilities of quantum devices.

title: Non-Linear Topological Structure for Probability Distribution Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear topological structure to probability distribution optimization, aiming to overcome the limitations of traditional probabilistic models in complex system modeling. We introduce a novel framework based on "拓扑进化" (Topological Evolution) algorithm, which iteratively constructs a topological structure and embeds the probability distribution within this structure. This approach enhances model performance, particularly in scenarios involving extreme conditions. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of topology to achieve dynamic probability adjustments and improve robustness. This work presents a new methodology with potential for significant advancements in modeling complex systems exhibiting non-linear dynamics and sensitivities.

title: Quantum Computing-Based Cryptographic Protocol Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the potential for optimizing cryptographic protocols by leveraging the capabilities of quantum computing. Traditional cryptographic schemes are increasingly vulnerable to attacks from classical computers, particularly those utilizing Shor's algorithm for factoring large numbers and the Generalized Commitment problem. This work investigates how quantum algorithms can be strategically employed to circumvent these vulnerabilities and enhance the security of existing protocols. Specifically, we examine the use of quantum annealing and quantum simulation to address computational bottlenecks within key exchange protocols, digital signatures, and encryption algorithms. The core claim is that exploiting quantum computing's properties can lead to optimized cryptographic protocols, ultimately improving security. The mechanism involves tackling the limitations of classical computations within these protocols. We propose several avenues for integrating quantum techniques, including quantum key distribution (QKD) enhancements and post-quantum cryptography (PQC) acceleration. The research contributes a novel perspective for future cryptographic developments, offering a pathway to secure communications in the face of evolving computational threats.

title: Dynamic Network Topology Optimization via Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamic optimization of network topology using evolutionary algorithms. Traditional network topology design is typically a static process, failing to adapt to fluctuating traffic demands or evolving system requirements. This research proposes a novel framework that employs evolutionary algorithms to continuously adjust network topology in real-time, achieving optimal performance. The core idea centers on utilizing algorithms like Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to iteratively refine network configurations. The methodology focuses on minimizing key performance indicators (KPIs) such as latency, packet loss, and congestion. The system considers factors like link capacity, node processing capabilities, and network topology constraints. The research demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of this dynamic approach through a theoretical framework and outlines potential future directions, including integration with real-world network monitoring systems and the implementation of more sophisticated adaptation strategies. This work addresses a critical gap in network design, offering a responsive and adaptable solution for optimizing network performance in dynamic environments.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Coding (QEIC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel information coding scheme, termed Quantum Entanglement Information Coding (QEIC), leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim is to achieve instantaneous information transmission surpassing the limitations imposed by classical physics. The proposed mechanism utilizes multi-particle entanglement to design a coding protocol where the measurement of one particle instantaneously determines the state of other entangled particles. This approach fundamentally differs from existing quantum information coding methods by directly exploiting the inherent correlations within entangled systems, potentially leading to information transfer exceeding the speed of light. The theoretical framework outlines the key components of the QEIC protocol, including entanglement generation, particle selection, and measurement strategies, demonstrating its feasibility and highlighting its potential implications for advanced communication and computation. The presented methodology offers a distinct pathway for exploring the boundaries of information transfer and harnessing the power of quantum mechanics.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Memory Storage
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed memory storage leveraging the phenomenon of quantum entanglement. The core claim is to achieve long-range, high-capacity, and low-latency distributed storage by exploiting entanglement. The mechanism involves establishing and maintaining multi-party quantum entanglement, encoding information within these entangled states, and utilizing the unique properties of entanglement for data transmission and storage, eliminating the need for classical communication channels. This approach addresses the bandwidth and latency limitations inherent in traditional distributed storage systems, capitalizing on the fundamental properties of quantum mechanics for enhanced information storage capabilities. The theoretical framework and key concepts are presented, outlining the potential for significant advancements in data storage technology. We explore the challenges and opportunities associated with building such a system, focusing on entanglement generation, distribution, and manipulation. The presented model offers a fundamentally different paradigm for data storage, promising substantial improvements in performance and scalability. ---

title: Probability and Linear Algebra Convergence: A Framework for Complex System Modeling
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic integration of probability logic and linear algebra, proposing a novel framework for studying and modeling complex systems, particularly within the realms of optimization and decision-making. The core mechanism centers around combining the probabilistic nature of probability distributions and probability theory with the computational power of linear algebra. This integration aims to provide a more flexible and robust toolset for tackling intricate systems, leveraging linear algebra's capabilities for probabilistic calculations and predictive modeling. The paper details the proposed framework, outlining its key components, potential applications, and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this convergence.

title: Adaptive Algorithms Optimized by Active Feedback
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithm optimization utilizing active feedback mechanisms. The core idea revolves around constructing a system capable of continuously monitoring and interpreting its environment, dynamically adjusting its internal parameters based on this feedback. This contrasts with traditional optimization methods that rely solely on predefined rules or static training datasets. The system's ability to adapt to changing conditions is central to its design, aiming to improve overall performance and robustness. We present a framework for implementing this active feedback loop, detailing the data collection, analysis, and parameter adjustment processes. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, focusing on the potential for enhanced adaptability across various algorithmic domains. The primary goal is to establish a methodology for creating algorithms that are not just trained, but actively learn and adjust their behavior in real-time. The research highlights the potential for significant improvements in algorithm performance and resilience when confronted with dynamic and unpredictable environments.

title: 基于自适应矩阵的量子算法设计
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive matrix techniques to quantum algorithm design, aiming to enhance the performance of existing quantum algorithms through dynamic parameter adjustment. Traditional quantum algorithm design often relies on static parameters, which can limit efficiency and accuracy. This research introduces a novel framework predicated on adaptive matrix adjustments, allowing the algorithm to optimize its performance based on the specific characteristics of the problem being addressed. The core mechanism centers around modifying the matrix parameters during the algorithm execution, effectively mitigating errors and enhancing the algorithm's overall effectiveness. We present a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the potential benefits of this approach.

title: Automated Hardware Security Vulnerability Discovery via Program Synthesis
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to hardware security vulnerability discovery by leveraging program synthesis techniques. The core idea is to automatically generate hardware circuits from high-level specifications and then analyze these circuits for potential vulnerabilities. This process combines formal verification with program synthesis, coupled with symbolic execution and coverage analysis, to achieve automated vulnerability detection. The resulting system offers a significant improvement over traditional manual inspection methods and provides a proactive defense against emerging hardware threats. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework, highlighting its potential for scaling security analysis across diverse hardware architectures. This research contributes to a more robust and resilient hardware ecosystem by automating the identification of vulnerabilities before deployment.

title: A large language model-based agent system for interactive large-scale project scheduling
abstract: Abstract Advanced optimization techniques generate highly complex schedules for large-scale engineering projects. While large language models have recently emerged as a transformative alternative for project scheduling, two primary hurdles must be overcome to realize a high-precision framework: performance degradation in large-scale projects and the functional separation between planning and analysis. To address these challenges, we propose an on-premises autonomous large language model agent system designed to raise open-source models to a level of accuracy that makes them a practical choice for industrial scheduling. Orchestrated within a LangGraph-based framework that uses the reasoning and acting paradigm, the agent facilitates a virtuous cycle in which plan generation and analytical feedback reinforce each other. To handle large-scale projects accurately, the agent uses a graph retrieval-augmented generation approach that combines local and global search over a knowledge graph of the schedule. It pairs this retrieval with analysis, modification, and optimization tools. Retrieval extracts only the relevant portion of the schedule, while the tools run schedule-wide computations that retrieval alone cannot perform, such as aggregation across all activities in the schedule. In a case study on real-world schedule data, the framework raised the accuracy of open-source backbones to about 90% on the large-scale schedule. By contrast, tool-free baselines struggled regardless of model: open-source models could not fit the schedule within their context window, and even a long-context commercial model (Gemini) reached only 41%. This points to the absence of tools, rather than the context window’s capacity, as the main bottleneck, a finding our component-wise ablation supports. Although this work was evaluated on a single project type at one shipyard, it demonstrates how large language models can become intelligent partners. It also provides a reference point for artificial intelligence-driven support in industrial scheduling and for similar work in other domains.

Although this work was evaluated on a single project type at one shipyard, it demonstrates how large language models can become intelligent partners. It also provides a reference point for artificial intelligence-driven support in industrial scheduling and for similar work in other domains.

title: GhostSplat: Input-Triggered Backdoors for Multi-View-Consistent 3D Content Manipulation in Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting
abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) reconstructs a 3D scene from sparse images in one forward pass. Its shared pretrained weights also expose a supply-chain attack surface. Existing Neural Radiance Field and 3DGS backdoors modify individual scenes and activate at selected viewpoints; they do not install persistent behavior in shared generator weights. We introduce GhostSplat, an input-triggered backdoor that installs such behavior in feed-forward 3DGS. A low-amplitude pattern added to the input images causes the poisoned generator to render an attacker-chosen payload on unseen victim scenes. Anchoring the payload to a 3D point and reprojecting it into each target view makes the payload multi-view consistent. Exact projection onto the generator's representation-specific consistency set leaves a realized payload unchanged because the output already belongs to that set. The GhostSplat training framework succeeds across three architectures (MVSplat, pixelSplat, DepthSplat) and two datasets (RealEstate10K, ACID). Its strongest evaluated injection and deletion settings reach 96% and 100% ASR, respectively, with zero observed false positives while surviving JPEG, blur, and resampling. Defenses that use only that exact projection are therefore insufficient; effective mitigation requires information or intervention beyond same-set consistency projection.

title: Effective Graph and Rank-based Contextual Embeddings for Textual and Multimedia Data
abstract: In a data-driven world, efficiently organizing and mapping relationships between objects is crucial. Graphs are powerful tools for modeling these connections, being widely used in social networks, telecommunications, and biology. However, graph-based methods often face high computational costs, particularly in memory and space usage. To address this, graph embedding techniques, also referred to as Network Representation Learning, encode graph information into lower-dimensional representations while preserving structural aspects. Traditional methods, however, lack interpretable dimensions. RaDE (Rank Diffusion Embedding) introduces a new approach using rank-based information, with a key step being the selection of a representative subset of nodes to provide interpretability for its dimensions and improve retrieval tasks. Despite its potential, RaDE's original proposal did not fully explore the effectiveness of representative subset selection across different classes or evaluate embeddings in tasks like classification and clustering. Inspired by RaDE, this work introduces GRaCE (Graph and Rank-based Contextual Embeddings), a fully unsupervised framework that generates interpretable embeddings by leveraging robust rank-based measures for representative subset selection and node embedding. GRaCE surpasses RaDE and Original Features across diverse datasets, including textual and image collections, excelling in retrieval, classification, and clustering tasks, considering state-of-the-art Transformer models as feature descriptors and Graph Convolutional Networks models in classification tasks.

title: Understanding Human Acceptance of Explainable AI in Automated Aesthetic Evaluation: A Multi-Study Investigation of Advice Taking and Explanation Requirements
abstract: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has been increasingly applied in image aesthetic quality evaluation. However, it remains unclear how perceived explainability influences users’ decision adoption and what specific explanation requirements shape this perception. This study develops and tests a multi-stage model of XAI-supported human–AI decision-making in aesthetic evaluation based on Task–Technology Fit theory with a self-developed AI aesthetic evaluation system and PLS-SEM analysis (N = 494). Our findings reveal that perceived explainability does not exert a direct effect on perceived fairness, but influences it indirectly through two underlying psychological mechanisms: functional understanding and affective satisfaction. Furthermore, perceived fairness serves as a critical mediating mechanism linking explainability perceptions to decision outcomes. Extending this framework, a second online questionnaire study(N = 313) investigates the specific explanation requirements of the users in AI-assisted aesthetic evaluation. The results reveal seven categories of explanation needs and develop a corresponding question bank to guide the design and evaluation of XAI systems. This study contributes to a unified theoretical understanding of explainable human–AI decision-making in aesthetic quality evaluation and provides practical guidance for researchers, developers, and organizations designing XAI-assisted aesthetic quality evaluation systems.

title: Impact of Multi-Task Intermediate Training on mT5's Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Performance
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the impact of combining multiple English intermediate tasks (e.g., NLI, QA, NER) on mT5's zero-shot cross-lingual EXACT match performance compared to single-task intermediate training, measured by XTREME-M benchmark accuracy? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.3/10.

title: The Price of Being Wrong: A Narrative Review of Loss Functions and Minimization, from Least Squares to Statistical Learning Theory
abstract: The loss function is machine learning's pricing of error: the function that measures a prediction's wrongness and whose expectation the learner minimizes---and its literature runs from the astronomers' least squares to the statistical learning theory's risk. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of that pricing, from Legendre's 1805 least squares and Gauss's 1809 probabilistic foundation---the errors' quadratic price justified by the Gaussian law---through Fisher's 1922 mathematical foundations of theoretical statistics, which made likelihood the estimation's criterion, Cox's 1958 regression of binary sequences, which fixed the logistic loss's model, Huber's 1964 robust estimation, which bounded the quadratic's sensitivity, Vapnik's 1998 statistical learning theory, which split empirical from structural risk, Cortes and Vapnik's 1995 support-vector networks, whose hinge loss carries margins, Rousseeuw's 1984 least median of squares, Boyd and Vandenberghe's 2004 convex optimization, Nesterov's 2004 introductory lectures, Rosasco, De Vito, Caponnetto, Piana, and Verri's 2004 comparison of the loss functions' statistical properties, and Goodfellow, Bengio, and Courville's 2016 Deep Learning, which codified the modern practice. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the quadratic heritage, in which the Gaussian's pricing governed from the comets to the regressions; robustness and margins, in which the loss's tails and the margin's geometry were engineered against error's extremes; and the risk framework, in which empirical, structural, and convex analysis gave the minimization its guarantees. It is concluded that the loss function is learning's economic core---every learner an argument about what wrongness costs.

title: Self-Organizing Quantum Networks
abstract: Quantum networks offer the potential for unparalleled security and information exchange, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. However, current quantum communication protocols face significant challenges due to the inherent fragility of quantum states and the difficulty of maintaining entanglement over long distances. This paper explores the design of a novel Self-Organizing Quantum Network (SONQN) that utilizes quantum entanglement for enhanced key distribution and communication, aiming to overcome these limitations. We propose a network architecture predicated on the self-organizing nature of entangled particles, focusing on protocols that minimize decoherence and maximize entanglement fidelity. This research delves into the fundamental principles underpinning SONQN, detailing the mechanism of entanglement-driven network formation, focusing on key operational parameters, and exploring potential improvements for scalability and robustness. The core claim is that this network design offers significantly improved efficiency and security compared to existing approaches, paving the way for more reliable quantum communication.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Networks for Robust Representation Learning in Noisy Data
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to representation learning in the presence of noisy data using Hierarchical Bayesian Networks (HBNs). Traditional Bayesian Networks often falter when dealing with highly correlated data streams, resulting in unstable inference outcomes. The core idea presented here is to construct an HBN with a layered structure, where higher-level nodes represent abstract concepts, and lower-level nodes represent specific features. Hierarchical priors are then introduced to model dependencies between these levels, effectively mitigating the impact of noisy observations and fostering robust representation learning. We demonstrate that this hierarchical structure significantly enhances robustness and accuracy compared to standard Bayesian Networks, particularly in scenarios characterized by complex dependencies and significant noise. The theoretical framework is presented, along with a discussion of key parameters and their influence on the model's behavior. The effectiveness of the HBN approach is illustrated through a conceptual example, highlighting the improved ability to capture underlying relationships within the data while remaining resilient to noise. Future research directions, including the incorporation of different prior distributions and the application of the HBN framework to diverse datasets, are also suggested.

title: 基于动态网络结构的自适应图灵机
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to designing a self-optimizing adaptive Turing machine, leveraging a dynamic network structure. Traditional Turing machines are static in their architecture, limiting their computational power. We introduce a core mechanism that dynamically adjusts the network's topology and connection strength based on input data and computation, enabling the machine to self-optimize and achieve enhanced inference capabilities. This design addresses a critical limitation of existing Turing machines by introducing a self-correcting and adaptable architecture. The paper details the core architecture, the underlying optimization algorithm, and preliminary results demonstrating the machine's ability to successfully execute complex logic sequences. The goal is to provide a foundation for more sophisticated and adaptable computational systems.

title: Contextualized Adversarial Robustness via Distributed Representation Learning
abstract: Adversarial robustness in deep neural networks remains a significant challenge, primarily addressed through static defense mechanisms that often prove brittle against evolving attack strategies. This research proposes a novel approach to adversarial robustness that dynamically adapts to contextual information. We introduce a distributed representation learning model designed to generate contextualized embeddings of input data. These embeddings capture the surrounding context, enabling the model to learn and apply defenses tailored to the specific situation. Our approach shifts the focus from static defenses to a dynamic, adaptive system, leveraging distributed representations for enhanced robustness. This method demonstrates improved resilience against adversarial attacks compared to traditional static defenses, highlighting the importance of contextual awareness in building robust deep learning systems. The core contribution lies in the learned contextual embeddings and the subsequent dynamic defense strategy they enable. We evaluate the proposed method against various attack scenarios and demonstrate its superior performance in maintaining accuracy against adversarial perturbations. ---

title: Based on Multi-modal Context Dynamic Knowledge Graph Generation and Reasoning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to dynamic knowledge graph generation and reasoning by leveraging multi-modal contextual information. The core idea is to construct a knowledge graph that can dynamically update and adapt to changing environments through the integration of data from diverse sources, including text, images, audio, and sensors. We propose a framework utilizing deep learning models for modality-specific feature extraction followed by a unified representation learning stage employing meta-learning or transfer learning. This unified representation is then used to drive the construction and reasoning within the knowledge graph, facilitated by Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for node embedding, relation prediction, and path reasoning. The resulting system demonstrates enhanced accuracy and interpretability compared to traditional knowledge graph approaches reliant solely on single-modality data. We demonstrate the potential for real-time knowledge acquisition and robust inference in complex, uncertain, and dynamic scenarios. ---

title: The Role of Quantum Computing in High-Performance Computing: Algorithms, Integration, and Current Limitations
abstract: High-performance computing has relied on classical architectures to attack problems demanding large scale computation. Quantum computing offers a different model, and the question of how the two relate has become practically relevant as quantum hardware has matured. This report reviews the case for integrating quantum processors into HPC environments as accelerators rather than replacements. It surveys the algorithmic families where quantum advantage is expected factoring, unstructured search, Hamiltonian simulation, and certain optimization problems and states the complexity relationships accurately rather than in the loose terms common in non-technical discussion. It then reviews the obstacles that currently separate demonstration from deployment: decoherence, gate error rates, the overhead of quantum error correction, and the cost of classical quantum data movement. This is an expository review and presents no new results.

title: Post-quantum Public-key Cryptosystem from Topological Conjugacy in Mapping Class Groups
abstract: This paper proposes a topology-based post-quantum public-key cryptosystem constructed from the Topological Conjugacy Search Problem in Mapping Class Groups (TCSP-MCG).The scheme is formulated as a non-Abelian ElGamal-type construction over mapping class groups, where the public key is generated from a conjugate pseudo-Anosov mapping class and the secret key is the hidden conjugator.Plaintexts, or fixed-length encapsulation seeds in the KEM-compatible mode, are injectively embedded into an abelian subgroup generated by commuting Dehn twists, while the non-Abelian group mask is produced through exponentiation.The security model designed through an explicit game-based IND-CPA analysis under TCSP-MCG search hardness, structured-key indistinguishability, decisional mask indistinguishability, and fixed-length encoding regularity.Classical, quantum, and geometric-group attacks are evaluated through direct search, meet-in-the-middle search, length-based heuristics, homological and traintrack invariant pruning, centralizer attacks, normal-form leakage, and non-Abelian Fourier-type attacks.A concrete serialization model, generator indexing rule, deterministic reduction procedure, capacity-constrained genus rule, bounded public-key normalization rule, bounded ciphertext normalization rule, and executable reproducibility artifact are provided to regenerate all numerical estimates.Representative profiles are labeled by nominal 128-, 192-, and 256bit post-quantum target levels, while their estimated quantum-amplified generic search exponents are intentionally higher, namely 192, 288, and 384 bits, respectively.These conservative profiles yield public-key sizes of 1536, 2304, and 3072 bits, secret-key sizes of 384, 576, and 768 bits, and encapsulation-ciphertext sizes of 1792, 2176, and 2560 bits, respectively.A KEM-oriented comparison with ML-KEM shows that the proposed profiles provide smaller serialized public keys, secret keys, ciphertexts, bandwidth, and persistent key-material storage under the stated representation model.These results indicate that TCSP-MCG offers a compact, mathematically distinct, and reproducible topology-based direction for post-quantum public-key cryptography.

title: Generative Fusion Decoding with MambaByte for Low-resource Regional Language Speech Recognition: A Case Study on Javanese and Sundanese
abstract: Javanese and Sundanese, spoken by over 110 million people, remain poorly served by automatic speech recognition.Zero-shot Whisper large-v3 attains word error rates of 58.16% and 61.64% on read-speech recordings of these languages-high enough to limit practical utility-yet supervised fine-tuning is infeasible where transcribed speech is unavailable.This work fuses a frozen Whisper large-v3 with MambaByte, a 972-million-parameter bytelevel selective state-space language model adapted to each language by LoRA continual pre-training on freely available text alone (235.5 MB Javanese; 120.9 MB Sundanese).A prefix-trie cache reduces each byte-level hypothesis extension to a constant-time state update, making the system tractable on a single GPU.With decoding hyperparameters selected on a small labelled set and no labelled speech used to adapt the language model, GFD reduces WER to 51.87% for Javanese (a statistically significant 6.29 percentage-point reduction) and 54.72% for Sundanese (a statistically significant 6.92 percentage-point reduction).

title: AI-Powered Chatbots for Customer Service in Banking
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered chatbots have become an integral component of digital transformation in the banking sector. These intelligent conversational agents utilize technologies such as Natural Language Processing (NLP), Machine Learning (ML), and Generative AI to provide efficient, personalized, and round-the-clock customer support. The increasing demand for instant banking services has encouraged financial institutions to deploy chatbots for handling customer inquiries, transaction assistance, financial guidance, and complaint resolution. This study examines the role of AI-powered chatbots in enhancing customer service within banking institutions by reviewing existing literature and proposing a conceptual framework for chatbot adoption. The study identifies key benefits such as improved operational efficiency, reduced service costs, enhanced customer satisfaction, and greater accessibility. Simultaneously, it highlights challenges associated with privacy, trust, cybersecurity, and ethical considerations. The findings suggest that AI chatbots significantly contribute to customer engagement and service innovation while emphasizing the necessity of integrating human support for complex banking interactions.

title: Independent Replication and a Reasoning-Model Stress-Test
abstract: An independent replication of the entropy-trajectory reliability signal, extended to a model class the original work did not test. We reproduce two published results on open-weight models over GSM8K and MATH-500: the dissociation between trajectory shape, measured as binary monotonicity, and trajectory magnitude, measured as total entropy drop; and the graded violation-count signal. We then stress-test whether the signal survives on reasoning-specialized, RL-distilled models, which emit longer and less structured chains whose step boundaries are not well defined, making segmentation itself part of the finding. A secondary analysis fits a triage filter combining violation count with final-answer confidence, to reduce the false-positive rate of the bare monotonicity flag. Preregistered before any confirmatory run. Harness, configurations, seeds and pinned model revisions are public.

title: SGPDFuse: Semantically-Guided Physics-Disentanglement General Multi-Modal Image Fusion
abstract: Multimodal image fusion (MMIF) aims to integrate complementary sensor data into a single representation that preserves intrinsic scene reality while eliminating environmental interferences. Most existing approaches rely on blind feature aggregation, which excels at signal accumulation but fails to distinguish essential content from physical degradations. We propose SGPDFuse, which bridges this gap by mapping inputs into a physics-disentangled structural representation via a Semantic-Physical Parametric Bridge (SPPB) built on pretrained vision foundation models, utilizing the Intrinsic-Variation principle to decouple invariant scene attributes from transient environmental factors. To guide this decomposition, we introduce a Semantic Alignment mechanism: we explicitly anchor the fused representation to salient semantic features in the same foundation model feature space via cosine similarity to preserve critical targets, while enforcing physical texture fidelity through Gram-matrix regularization to strictly eliminate unnatural artifacts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SGPDFuse achieves state-of-the-art performance across infrared-visible, multi-focus, and multi-exposure benchmarks using a single architecture.

title: An Explainable XGBoost–SHAP Framework for Social Vulnerability Assessment in Coastal Communities
abstract: Purpose – This exploratory pilot study aims to develop an interpretable machine learning framework for predicting social vulnerability in the coastal areas of Cilacap Regency, Indonesia. Design/methods/approach – The study utilized an optimised eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm integrated with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), based on socio-economic data collected from seven coastal sub-districts during 2024–2025. The dataset includes indicators such as poverty rate, population density, education level, and infrastructure accessibility. Due to the limited sample size (n = 7), model evaluation was conducted using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV). Findings – The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 94.2% and an AUC-ROC value of 0.96 within the experimental dataset. SHAP analysis indicates that socio-economic vulnerability and geographic isolation are among the most influential contributing factors. Research implications/limitations – Nevertheless, the findings should be cautiously interpreted because the limited regional dataset constrains broader generalisability. Despite these limitations, this study demonstrates the potential of integrating machine learning and XAI to provide interpretable and data-driven insights that may support policymakers in prioritising mitigation strategies for high-risk coastal communities. Originality/value – Social vulnerability is a critical component of disaster risk management, particularly in coastal regions where complex socio-economic factors interact dynamically. However, conventional approaches often fail to capture non-linear relationships and provide limited predictive interpretability.
